title: Quantum-Driven Neuromorphic Computing For Million-Qubit-Scale Workloads
authors: Adams Ivanov, Samer Rahmeh, Erick Giovani Sperandio Nascimento, Daniela Herrmann
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Apollo, a 10000 node p-qubit neuromorphic processor fabricated in 16 nm mixed signal CMOS and operating fully at room temperature with a typical analog core power envelope of about 0.5 W. Its fundamental element, the p-qubit, is a bistable stochastic unit whose continuous time state fluctuations are driven by integrated quantum entropy units that inject true quantum derived randomness. This enables ultrafast stochastic transitions at low energy while preserving a classical state representation. Apollo combines these p-qubits with a high degree Hyperion 256 interconnect topology, allowing efficient embedding of dense Ising and QUBO problems with substantially reduced minor embedding overhead compared with sparse annealing platforms. We show that, through the Suzuki Trotter correspondence, the equilibrium statistics and annealing dynamics of the p-qubit network reproduce key properties of transverse field quantum annealing without cryogenic cooling, long lived coherence, or microwave control. Beyond device level validation, Apollo is evaluated on a three dimensional spin glass benchmark previously used to study quantum advantage in superconducting annealers. Across 300 disorder realizations, Apollo reaches substantially lower ground state energies than reported cryogenic quantum annealing hardware, while remaining distinct from classical simulated annealing and simulated quantum annealing. A 350 nm release candidate device experimentally validates the core p-qubit dynamics, thermodynamic sampling correctness, and continuous time annealing behavior. These results establish Apollo as a room temperature, industrially scalable platform for quantum driven energy based optimization, probabilistic inference, generative modeling, and hybrid classical quantum workflows.
tldr: Apollo is a room-temperature neuromorphic processor using p-qubits driven by quantum entropy for stochastic optimization, mimicking quantum annealing without cryogenics.
motivation: To achieve quantum-like optimization performance at room temperature, avoiding the need for cryogenic cooling and long coherence times.
method: A 10,000-node p-qubit processor fabricated in 16nm CMOS, using integrated quantum entropy units for stochastic transitions and a Hyperion 256 interconnect for dense Ising/QUBO embedding.
result: Apollo reaches lower ground state energies on 3D spin glass benchmarks than cryogenic quantum annealers, while outperforming classical simulated annealing.
conclusion: The platform demonstrates industrially scalable, room-temperature quantum-driven optimization, with potential for hybrid classical-quantum workflows.

title: Theoretical Study For Generating Optical Gkp State Via A Single-Photon-Added Squeezed Vacuum
authors: Deriyan Senjaya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theoretical framework is developed to analyze the generation of the optical GKP state using a single-photon-added squeezed vacuum. This state, defined by the squeezing parameter [MATH], is injected into a 50:50 beam splitter, and the optical GKP state is obtained through conditional measurement at one output port. The single-photon-added squeezed vacuum is especially prominent in this context because it provides a simpler and more experimentally accessible ingredient than Schrodinger cat states, while conditional measurement ensures projection onto a state that closely approximates the finite-energy GKP form. Fidelity is employed to quantify this closeness, and the analysis demonstrates that the scheme achieves a maximum fidelity of 85% at a squeezing level of [MATH]. This performance surpasses approaches based on squeezed optical odd Schrodinger cat states, underscoring the single-photon-added squeezed vacuum as a practical and effective pathway toward fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate optical GKP states using single-photon-added squeezed vacuum and conditional measurement, achieving 85% fidelity.
motivation: GKP states are essential for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing, but existing generation methods are complex; this work aims for a simpler, more accessible approach.
method: A single-photon-added squeezed vacuum is injected into a 50:50 beam splitter; conditional measurement at one output port projects the other port into an approximate GKP state.
result: The scheme achieves a maximum fidelity of 85% at a specific squeezing level, outperforming methods based on squeezed odd Schrödinger cat states.
conclusion: The single-photon-added squeezed vacuum provides a practical and effective pathway for generating optical GKP states, advancing fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.

title: Graph Reinforcement Learning For Calibration-Aware Quantum Circuit Routing
authors: Yash Vardhan Tomar, Dheeraj Peddireddy, Vaneet Aggarwal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum circuit routing is a key step in compiling programs for noisy intermediate-scale quantum processors. Routes that appear efficient by standard overhead metrics can still lose fidelity when they pass through poorly calibrated couplers. We study a calibration-aware graph reinforcement-learning router that uses same-day IBM Heron r2 calibration data to choose hardware-edge SWAPs. We train the policy with proximal policy optimization and evaluate it with exact simulated fidelity across nine Munich Quantum Toolkit (MQT) Bench circuits and three calibration snapshots. Across these evaluations, pooled mean exact fidelity is [MATH], compared with [MATH] for SABRE-best20 and [MATH] for target-aware SABRE. Fidelity gains come with higher routed two-qubit counts and are concentrated in the 5q and 8q circuit families; under the fixed tree action graph, all 10q families favor SABRE-best20. Overall, our results show that calibration-aware learned routing can improve fidelity beyond gate-count-driven compilation.
tldr: A graph reinforcement learning approach for calibration-aware quantum circuit routing to improve fidelity on NISQ processors.
motivation: Standard quantum circuit routing optimizes for gate count but ignores coupler calibration, leading to fidelity loss; this work aims to incorporate calibration data into routing decisions.
method: Uses a graph reinforcement learning policy trained with proximal policy optimization, leveraging same-day calibration data from IBM Heron r2 to select SWAP operations.
result: Achieves higher exact simulated fidelity than SABRE-based baselines on small circuits (5q, 8q) but not on 10q circuits; fidelity gains come with increased two-qubit gate counts.
conclusion: Calibration-aware learned routing can improve fidelity for small circuits, but scalability and generalizability remain challenges.

title: On The Universal Commuting Dilation Constant

title: Effective Geometry And Position-Dependent Mass In Dual-$q$ Quantum Mechanics
authors: A. Makhlouf A. Boumali
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the deformed-derivative formalism introduced by Borges, with emphasis on the relation between the linear operator [MATH] and its nonlinear dual counterpart [MATH]. Directly inserting the dual derivative into the kinetic term leads to a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation and obscures the usual interpretation of superposition and probability. We show that this nonlinearity can be removed by a simultaneous transformation of the coordinate and of the wave function. The transformed problem is an ordinary linear Schr\"odinger equation in a deformed coordinate, and its representation in the physical coordinate is equivalent to a Hermitian position-dependent-mass (PDM) Hamiltonian. In this formulation, the deformation parameter [MATH] determines both the effective mass profile and the associated metric. The formalism is applied to the free particle, the infinite square well, the rectangular barrier, and the harmonic oscillator in the weak-deformation regime. Comparison with the nonadditive-translation approach of Costa Filho shows that the Borges dual-[MATH] framework provides an alternative route to the same effective geometric structure. For [MATH], the effective confinement length is reduced, which raises the bound-state spectrum and enhances tunneling; for [MATH], the effective length is increased, which lowers the spectrum and suppresses tunneling relative to the undeformed limit [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies a deformed-derivative formalism leading to a position-dependent-mass Hamiltonian, applied to simple quantum systems.
motivation: To resolve nonlinearity in a dual-q deformed Schrödinger equation by transforming to an effective linear equation with a deformed coordinate.
method: The authors apply a simultaneous coordinate and wavefunction transformation to convert the nonlinear equation into a linear one with a position-dependent mass, then solve for free particle, infinite well, barrier, and harmonic oscillator in the weak-deformation regime.
result: The deformation parameter modifies the effective confinement length, raising or lowering bound-state spectra and enhancing or suppressing tunneling compared to the undeformed case.
conclusion: The Borges dual-q framework provides an alternative geometric interpretation equivalent to a position-dependent mass Hamiltonian, but the work is primarily a mathematical extension without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quasi-Product States And Factor Types For The One-Dimensional Hard-Core Model
authors: Yuri Suhov Farrukh Mukhamedov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quasi-product state associated with the one-dimensional hard-core Gibbs measure. After coding the model by the topological Markov chain, we construct the standard path [MATH]-algebra of admissible hard-core words and show that the stationary Markov measure induces on it a faithful diagonal state in the sense of Evans. We then analyze the von Neumann algebra generated by the corresponding GNS representation. The resulting algebra is a hyperfinite factor, and its type is determined by the single parameter \(\kappa=q/p^2,\) where \(p&q\\ 1&0\) is the transition matrix of the Markov chain. title: The Formation Of Magnetic Reentrancy In The Ising Model On A Decorated Square Lattice
authors: F. A. Kassan-Ogly A. V. Zarubin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our work, based on an exact solution of the Ising model on a decorated square lattice with an arbitrary number of decorating spins, we have demonstrated the fundamental possibility of describing the phenomenon of multiple magnetic phase transitions (magnetic reentrancy) in the regime of competing exchange interactions. We analyzed the magnetic behavior of the system and established the conditions for the occurrence of magnetic reentrancy. We have determined the relationships of the model parameter under which the formation of one, three, and even five magnetic phase transitions is possible, which is confirmed by a complicated magnetic phase diagram. We have also proposed a unique method for finding critical temperatures that allows for the precise determination of their number and values, including those at extremely low temperatures.
tldr: This paper exactly solves the Ising model on a decorated square lattice to demonstrate multiple magnetic phase transitions (magnetic reentrancy) under competing interactions.
motivation: To understand the fundamental possibility of multiple magnetic phase transitions in a simple statistical mechanical model.
method: Exact solution of the Ising model on a decorated square lattice with arbitrary number of decorating spins, using transfer matrix or related techniques.
result: Conditions for one, three, or five magnetic phase transitions are established, and a method for precisely determining critical temperatures is proposed.
conclusion: Magnetic reentrancy can be described within the exactly solvable Ising model, providing a theoretical framework for multiple phase transitions.

title: Discrete Phase Symmetry Of Stationary States In Bichromatically Pumped Kerr Microresonators
authors: Boulat Nougmanov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bichromatically pumped Kerr microresonators exhibit phase bistability and multistability arising from four-wave mixing between pump and generated modes. Here we analyze the symmetry structure of stationary solutions in the coupled-mode description of such systems. We show that the two-pump coupled-mode equations are a particular case of a more general model with pumps placed at equally spaced modes. For this model, any stationary solution generates a finite family of stationary solutions through a discrete phase transformation. This transformation leaves the equations invariant and preserves the stability type of the corresponding stationary states. As a consequence, the possible stationary values of each individual mode form a regular polygon in the complex plane. The number of vertices is determined by the order of the mode index [MATH] in the group [MATH], where [MATH] is the separation between the pumped modes. Thus, the phase multistability structure depends not only on nonlinear dynamics but also on the arithmetic relation between the mode index and the pump separation. These results provide a simple symmetry-based explanation for the discrete phase structure observed in multimode Kerr resonators under bichromatic pumping.
tldr: This paper analyzes discrete phase symmetry in stationary states of bichromatically pumped Kerr microresonators, revealing a regular polygon structure in mode phases determined by arithmetic relations.
motivation: Understanding the symmetry and multistability structure in Kerr microresonators under bichromatic pumping is important for nonlinear optics and frequency comb generation.
method: The authors derive a general coupled-mode model for pumps at equally spaced modes and identify a discrete phase transformation that leaves the equations invariant, preserving stability.
result: Stationary solutions form families related by discrete phase rotations; the number of vertices in the phase polygon is determined by the mode index modulo the pump separation.
conclusion: The phase multistability in such systems is governed by a simple symmetry principle rooted in arithmetic relations, providing a unified explanation for observed discrete phase structures.

title: Explicit Quantum Circuit Simulation Of Nonlinear 1-Dimensional Fluid With Carleman-linearized Boltzmann Method
authors: Keita Kanno, Kazumasa Ueno, Hayato Higuchi, Morimasa Okamoto, Yuya Yoshizuru, Ryoya Ishimaru, Towa Takagi, Kentaro Sakamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computation of fluid dynamics has attracted growing attention as a key application of fault-tolerant quantum computers anticipated in the coming decade, with lattice Boltzmann methods emerging as a particularly promising approach. Explicit and efficient elementary-gate-level circuit simulations, however, have so far been demonstrated only in the linear case. Here we include the leading nonlinearity through second-order Carleman linearization of the one-dimensional Boltzmann equation, and demonstrate, via explicit quantum-circuit simulation, the preparation of the final-time state using a Taylor-expansion-based ODE solver based on the quantum singular value transformation. With this construction, we analyze the gate and qubit complexities, which scale logarithmically with the grid size, the nonlinearity captured by the higher-order Carleman linearization, and the practical utility of higher-order expansions in the Taylor ODE solver. The construction provides a concrete baseline for computational cost reduction and further developments such as extensions to higher dimensions, complex geometries, and the extraction of physical quantities, towards industrially useful quantum CFD.
tldr: This paper simulates nonlinear 1D fluid dynamics on a quantum computer using Carleman linearization and quantum singular value transformation.
motivation: Quantum simulation of fluid dynamics is a promising application for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but explicit circuit-level simulations have been limited to linear cases.
method: The authors apply second-order Carleman linearization to the 1D Boltzmann equation and use a Taylor-expansion-based ODE solver via quantum singular value transformation to prepare the final-time state.
result: Gate and qubit complexities scale logarithmically with grid size; the approach captures nonlinearity and demonstrates explicit quantum circuit simulation.
conclusion: This work provides a baseline for quantum computational fluid dynamics, with potential extensions to higher dimensions and complex geometries.

title: Beyond-Third-Order Quantum Coherence In Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy Via Order-Selective Isolation
authors: Xue Zhang, De-Ran Zhang, Hui Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in nonlinear spectroscopy is the order-selective readout of weak higher-order responses that spectrally overlap with dominant lower-order signals. This bottleneck is particularly severe in two-dimensional (2D) spectroscopy, where extending conventional phase-cycling schemes to higher orders rapidly increases measurement and analysis complexity. Here we introduce a computation-assisted strategy that combines rotating-frame acquisition with a frame-shift tracking algorithm to separate signals by their frame-dependent spectral shifts. In a rubidium vapor experiment, we use this approach to isolate a 7th-order nonlinear contribution from coexisting 3rd-order components, enabling direct access to higher-order quantum-coherence dynamics without sacrificing operation at comparatively high pulse intensities. The method is broadly compatible with multidimensional spectroscopy platforms and provides a practical route to probing many-body and collective ultrafast dynamics beyond third order.
tldr: A computation-assisted method to isolate higher-order quantum coherence signals in 2D spectroscopy.
motivation: Higher-order nonlinear signals in 2D spectroscopy are weak and overlap with dominant lower-order signals, making them difficult to measure.
method: Combines rotating-frame acquisition with a frame-shift tracking algorithm to separate signals by frame-dependent spectral shifts.
result: Successfully isolated a 7th-order nonlinear contribution from coexisting 3rd-order components in a rubidium vapor experiment.
conclusion: The method enables direct access to higher-order quantum-coherence dynamics without sacrificing pulse intensity, and is broadly compatible with multidimensional spectroscopy platforms.

title: Quantum Walk-based Optimisation For Capacitated Vehicle Routing With Homogeneous And Heterogeneous Fleets
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Aidan Smith, Callum Neill, Paulo Santos, Ugo Varetto, Jingbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) is an appealing candidate for quantum optimisation due to its combinatorial complexity and practical importance. However, the problem's constrained search space poses a challenge for such quantum algorithms. We introduce a quantum walk-based optimisation algorithm (QWOA) for the CVRP with homogeneous or heterogeneous vehicle fleets, addressing this challenge through a continuous-time quantum walk over a product space that coincides with combinatorial structures intrinsic to the CVRP solution space. Relative to the prior QWOA-based formulation, this approach reduces the per-layer gate complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] and supports a circuit parameterisation schedule generated by a fixed number of classical parameters. Exact state-vector simulation on instances with up to [MATH] customers and [MATH] vehicles demonstrates improved convergence to low-cost solutions using markedly fewer objective function evaluations, with the advantage broadening as problem size increases. These results identify structured product-space walks as a promising tool for optimisation over constrained combinatorial spaces.
tldr: This paper applies a quantum walk-based optimization algorithm to the capacitated vehicle routing problem, a classical combinatorial optimization problem.
motivation: The capacitated vehicle routing problem is combinatorially complex and practically important, making it a candidate for quantum optimization.
method: The authors introduce a continuous-time quantum walk over a product space that matches the combinatorial structure of the CVRP, reducing gate complexity and using a fixed number of classical parameters.
result: Exact state-vector simulations on instances with up to 12 customers and 4 vehicles show improved convergence to low-cost solutions with fewer objective function evaluations compared to prior QWOA formulations.
conclusion: Structured product-space quantum walks are a promising tool for optimization over constrained combinatorial spaces.

title: Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Induced By Spatial Noncommutativity
authors: Su-Peng Kou Zheng Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In all known schemes for the non-Hermitian skin effect, the non-Hermitian ingredient that drives the skin localization, whether asymmetric hopping or gain and loss, is invariably introduced by hand as an independent model parameter along the skin direction. Here we show that when two spatial coordinates do not commute, the skin effect can break free of this paradigm: a gain-loss potential applied along one coordinate automatically generates non-reciprocity along the other through the coordinate noncommutativity, driving all eigenstates to pile up exponentially at a boundary. We term this phenomenon the noncommutative skin effect. The inverse skin length is proportional to the noncommutativity parameter and is given by an analytic formula, exact in the thermodynamic limit and verified by exact diagonalization of lattice models; the reflection symmetry of the imaginary potential furnishes an exact criterion for the presence or absence of the effect, valid rigorously for finite-size systems. For a sinusoidal imaginary potential, the skin direction of all eigenstates flips collectively at parameter points fixed purely by geometry. Because the flip point is independent of the potential strength, the reversal constitutes a zero-crossing measurement scheme intrinsically robust against systematic errors, from which the noncommutativity parameter can be extracted directly. The qualitative transition of the eigenstates from uniform to exponentially localized renders the effect a nonperturbative probe of spatial noncommutativity, and the Peierls-phase structure of its lattice model is in principle accessible to cold-atom synthetic dimensions, photonic resonators, and topolectrical circuits.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-Hermitian skin effect driven by spatial noncommutativity, where a gain-loss potential along one coordinate induces non-reciprocity along another.
motivation: To find a new mechanism for the non-Hermitian skin effect that does not require manually introducing non-Hermitian terms along the skin direction.
method: The authors use analytic formulas in the thermodynamic limit and exact diagonalization of lattice models to demonstrate the effect, and propose a zero-crossing measurement scheme.
result: The inverse skin length is proportional to the noncommutativity parameter, and the skin direction flips collectively at geometry-determined points, providing a robust probe of spatial noncommutativity.
conclusion: The noncommutative skin effect offers a nonperturbative probe of spatial noncommutativity and is accessible in cold-atom, photonic, and circuit platforms.

title: Generalized Norm Retrieval And Generalized Phase Retrieval In Hilbert Spaces
authors: Vahid Sadri Gholamreza Rahimlou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce generalized phase retrieval (briefly, g-phase retrieval) and generalized norm retrieval (briefly, g-norm retrieval). Then, we present some properties of these concepts in Hilbert spaces, with special emphasis on R^n. Finally, the stability of g-norm retrieval for R^n is proved.
tldr: The paper introduces generalized phase retrieval and generalized norm retrieval in Hilbert spaces, focusing on mathematical properties and stability in R^n.
motivation: To extend the concepts of phase retrieval and norm retrieval to a more general framework in Hilbert spaces.
method: The authors define g-phase retrieval and g-norm retrieval, derive their properties, and prove stability results for g-norm retrieval in R^n.
result: New definitions and basic properties of generalized retrieval concepts are established, along with a stability theorem for g-norm retrieval.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical foundation for generalized retrieval problems but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: A $q$-analogue Of The Rational Normal Curve And Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Valentina Astore, Martino Borello, Alain Couvreur, Flavio Salizzoni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relationship between linear codes in the Hamming metric and projective algebraic varieties has led to deep interactions between coding theory and algebraic geometry, with classical examples such as Reed-Solomon codes and the rational normal curve. On the other hand, the sum-rank metric has recently gained attention due to applications in network coding, distributed storage, and post-quantum cryptography, with linearized Reed-Solomon codes emerging as optimal constructions. Despite recent advances, their structural and geometric properties are still not fully understood, and existing distinguishers remain limited. In this paper, we develop a geometric framework for linearized Reed-Solomon codes by considering a [MATH]-analogue of the rational normal curve. This yields a geometric characterization for certain parameter choices and reveals that the corresponding sets of points satisfy unexpectedly many [MATH]-degree hypersurface conditions. Our approach extends Schur-product-based techniques from the Hamming and rank-metric settings to the sum-rank metric case. Finally, we study the Hilbert function of the associated coordinate ring, providing a detailed description of its behavior and identifying its regularity, which also sheds new light on Gabidulin codes.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for linearized Reed-Solomon codes using a q-analogue of the rational normal curve, focusing on sum-rank metric codes.
motivation: To better understand the structural and geometric properties of linearized Reed-Solomon codes, which are optimal in the sum-rank metric but lack geometric characterization.
method: Introduces a q-analogue of the rational normal curve, extends Schur-product techniques from Hamming and rank-metric settings to sum-rank metric, and studies the Hilbert function of the associated coordinate ring.
result: Provides a geometric characterization for certain parameter choices, reveals unexpected hypersurface conditions, and describes the Hilbert function's behavior and regularity.
conclusion: The geometric framework sheds new light on linearized Reed-Solomon codes and Gabidulin codes, but the work is primarily in algebraic coding theory with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Calculus Of Apartness Over Separoids: Effective Convex Representation, Stratified Conservativity, And The Complexity Of Entailment
authors: Baris Basaran Faruk Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every finite family of compact convex bodies in Euclidean space induces an apartness relation between disjoint index sets: two sets are apart when the convex hulls of the corresponding unions are disjoint. This paper studies the finite theory obtained by taking apartness as the primitive relation. Its basic laws are symmetry, bilateral subsumption, and vacuity, equivalently the separation-polarity form of acyclic separoids. The main contribution is an effective rational realization theorem with uniform margins and the exact consequence theory it supports. Every finite apartness separoid is realized by rational polytopes whose coordinates are indexed by maximal separations. Maximal separations and minimal Radon partitions can be enumerated from a full table, generators, or a membership oracle; the coordinate values have controlled bit height; and each coordinate records a readable certificate of one maximal separation. The realization separates every apart pair with clearance at least 2, remains correct under outer parallel enlargement by any radius below 1, and yields full-dimensional convex bodies after thickening. The distance-function layer records standard convex-analytic stability through Lipschitz comparison, monotonicity under inclusion, and outer parallel bodies. On the logical side, positive entailment is exactly one-premise subsumption. Boolean consequence over Euclidean scenes is sound, complete, and decidable; satisfiability is NP-complete, validity is coNP-complete, and positive entailment is linear for sorted encodings. A stratification theorem shows that Boolean reasoning introduces no new atomic apartness beyond separoid closure. Fixed-dimensional consequence relations form a strictly decreasing hierarchy that stabilizes in dimension n minus 1 for n sites.
tldr: This paper studies the combinatorial and logical theory of apartness relations over separoids, with a focus on convex geometry and computational complexity.
motivation: To develop a finite axiomatic theory of apartness as a primitive relation and provide effective realizations using rational polytopes.
method: The authors define apartness separoids, prove an effective rational realization theorem with uniform margins, and analyze the complexity of entailment problems.
result: Every finite apartness separoid is realized by rational polytopes; Boolean consequence is decidable with NP-complete satisfiability and coNP-complete validity; positive entailment is linear.
conclusion: The work establishes a complete logical and geometric framework for apartness relations, with implications for convex geometry and computational complexity.

title: Flux-explicit Cheeger Bounds For Magnetic Laplacians On Compact Metric Graphs
authors: Bj\"orn Dahlke
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let (\Gamma) be a finite compact connected metric graph and let (A\in L^\infty(\Gamma)) be a real magnetic potential. The magnetic Laplacian (H_A) with standard vertex conditions is defined by the closed quadratic form [ q_A[u]=\sum_e\int_e |(-i\partial_x-A_e)u_e|^2,dx. ] A magnetic Cheeger constant is introduced by adding to the usual boundary term the frustration index of the potential on subgraphs. The first point of the paper is that, on a metric graph, this frustration index is exactly a finite dimensional (\ell^1) flux distance determined by the periods of (A) on cycles. Consequently the Cheeger constant can be written directly in terms of Aharonov Bohm fluxes. We prove a Cheeger type lower bound for the bottom of the spectrum and derive the corresponding explicit lower estimate in terms of the distance of the global cycle flux vector from the integral flux lattice. The estimate also gives (L^2) decay bounds for the magnetic heat semigroup and for the magnetic energy. The constants are not asserted to be sharp; the emphasis is on the flux dependence and on the self contained metric graph formulation.
tldr: This paper proves Cheeger-type lower bounds for the spectrum of magnetic Laplacians on compact metric graphs, with explicit dependence on Aharonov-Bohm fluxes.
motivation: To understand how magnetic fluxes affect the spectral gap and heat decay on metric graphs, extending classical Cheeger inequalities to the magnetic setting.
method: Introduces a magnetic Cheeger constant incorporating a frustration index, which is shown to be an ℓ1 flux distance determined by periods of the magnetic potential on cycles, then derives lower bounds using variational techniques.
result: Obtains explicit lower bounds for the bottom of the spectrum in terms of the distance of the global cycle flux vector from the integral flux lattice, and corresponding L2 decay bounds for the magnetic heat semigroup.
conclusion: The spectral gap and heat decay on metric graphs are controlled by the magnetic flux, with the Cheeger constant expressed directly via Aharonov-Bohm fluxes.

title: King Function For Shifted Gaussian: Laguerre Structure, Spectral Theory And Density
authors: Zhe Gao Yanpeng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study King function arising as radial kernels in the laboratory-frame spherical harmonic expansion of shifted Gaussian distributions. We first clarify their relation with the co-moving Laguerre hierarchy by means of a King--Laguerre expansion. We then derive the King differential equation and show that the associated self-adjoint operator in a Gaussian-weighted Hilbert space is unitarily equivalent to the free radial Schr\"odinger operator on the half-line. This yields the spectral representation and generalized eigenfunction. Finally, we prove that real-parameter King function, lies in the resolvent set, form a dense non-orthogonal system in a natural radial velocity space, providing an approximation-theoretic basis for King mixture representations. Weighted \(L^1\)-integrability criteria and closed-form moment formulas are also derived, justifying the normalization of King function.
tldr: This paper studies the King function arising from shifted Gaussian distributions, focusing on its spectral theory and approximation properties.
motivation: To understand the mathematical structure of King functions and their role in representing shifted Gaussian distributions.
method: Derives a King differential equation, shows unitary equivalence to the free radial Schrödinger operator, and analyzes spectral properties.
result: Establishes a King-Laguerre expansion, spectral representation, and density results for King functions in a weighted Hilbert space.
conclusion: The King function forms a dense non-orthogonal system useful for mixture representations, with closed-form moment formulas.

title: A Mathematical Theory Of Value: A Synthesis On Goal-directed Agency Under Resource Constraints
authors: Cheng Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose that value -- the quantity goal-directed agents create, destroy, and exchange -- is a lawful structural quantity in the same category as information. Following Shannon's method, we make one ruthless abstraction: value is the rate at which an agent converts a resource into goal-progress, relative to a frame fixed by its goal. A scale-invariance axiom forces a logarithmic measure, [MATH]; compounding of a reinvested resource forces the same form via the ergodicity argument of Peters (2019). The two routes are kin rather than independent; their agreement is a consistency check, not an over-determination. We derive a coding theorem of value: [MATH], achieved by Bayes-proportional allocation; realized value decomposes as [MATH], identifying misalignment with measurable waste. For populations, value is frame-relative while price is frame-independent; a fleet that pools its resource and fuses its perception inherits the ceiling [MATH] (a corollary; an earlier sum-form claim was wrong and is corrected in v5). A dynamical layer yields an is/ought asymmetry from which alignment emerges as a control-stability condition with a closed-form residual. We test the single-frame laws on live language models in a pre-registered scale-up: perception mutual information tracks realized capability rather than parameter count (Spearman [MATH] pooled over 30 model[MATH]domain points), out-of-sample [MATH] tracks [MATH], and over-confidence is measurable dissipation; a further pre-registered test shows the bridge is shape-invariant across four task shapes ([MATH], slope 0.953). None of the mechanisms is individually new -- generalized Kelly, Armstrong & Mindermann (2018), classical control; the contribution is their unification and the governance mapping (incentive design over oversight) that follows.
tldr: This paper proposes a mathematical theory of value as a structural quantity analogous to information, applied to goal-directed agents under resource constraints.
motivation: To formalize value in a way that unifies concepts from information theory, economics, and control theory, and to derive laws governing value creation and exchange.
method: The author uses axiomatic reasoning (scale invariance, compounding) to derive a logarithmic measure of value, a coding theorem, and a decomposition into alignment and waste, with empirical tests on language models.
result: The theory yields a logarithmic value measure, a coding theorem achieved by Bayes-proportional allocation, and empirical validation showing perception mutual information tracks capability in language models.
conclusion: Value is a lawful structural quantity; the framework unifies known mechanisms and provides a governance mapping for incentive design.

title: Candidate Overtone Shear Horizontal Saw Resonators In Thin-film Lithium Niobate For Intermodal Acousto-optic Modulation
authors: Wenbing Jiang, Xuankai Xu, Yu Guo, Boyu Zhang, Lihui Jin, Xiao Chen, Tao Wu, Libing Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The merits of thin-film surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices are pivotal to develop the high-performance intermodal acousto-optic modulators. In this work, we have proposed shear-horizontal (SH) SAW resonators for anticipated intermodal acousto-optic modulation on the thin-film lithium niobate platform. Through optimization of the cut angle of LN films, the SAW wavelength, and the thickness of interdigital transducer (IDT) electrodes, the calculated acousto-optic overlap factors utilizing SH0 modes are improved by more than an order of magnitude compared with those of Rayleigh modes. Furthermore, we have fabricated and characterized three kinds of proof-of-principle SH0 mode devices without/with grating reflectors. The electromechanical coupling coefficients (keff^2) and quality factors (Q) in the overtone resonators with grating reflectors are systematically evaluated, featuring the highest Q of 843 with the compromised keff^2 of 0.96%-4.72%. The results reveal that the temperature coefficients of frequency (TCF) of Rayleigh modes vary across various overtones, whereas the SH0 modes exhibit TCFs in the range of 32.3-68.9 ppm/C. Our fabricated SH0-mode overtone resonators demonstrate the capability of operating at power levels up to 29 dBm without electrode damage, offering a promising paradigm for robust and high-efficiency intermodal acousto-optic modulators with potential applications in integrated optical signal processing, microwave photonics,and quantum information technologies.
tldr: This paper presents shear-horizontal SAW resonators on thin-film lithium niobate for intermodal acousto-optic modulation, with potential applications in quantum information technologies.
motivation: To improve the performance of intermodal acousto-optic modulators by optimizing shear-horizontal SAW resonators on thin-film lithium niobate.
method: Optimization of cut angle, SAW wavelength, and IDT electrode thickness; fabrication and characterization of SH0 mode devices with grating reflectors.
result: Acousto-optic overlap factors improved by >10x over Rayleigh modes; highest Q of 843 with keff^2 of 0.96%-4.72%; TCF of SH0 modes 32.3-68.9 ppm/°C; power handling up to 29 dBm.
conclusion: SH0-mode overtone resonators offer a promising platform for robust and high-efficiency intermodal acousto-optic modulators, with potential in quantum information technologies.

title: Masked Neural Detection For Constrained Channel Coding In Molecular Communication
authors: Ozgur B. Akan Melih \c{s}ahin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular communication (MC) suffers from severe diffusion memory because molecules released for one symbol may arrive during later symbols. Neural sequence detectors, especially sliding bidirectional recurrent neural networks (SBRNNs), can substantially outperform threshold detectors in such channels. This raises a central question for MC channel coding: does a code whose advantage was established under threshold detection retain it when both coded and uncoded transmission are evaluated with neural detection? This letter answers this question for run-length-limited ISI-mitigation (RLIM) codes, a class of constrained codes previously shown to provide large BER gains in MC. Across the tested operating points, the best RLIM-SBRNN receiver beats the best uncoded receiver, chosen between threshold and SBRNN detection, in [MATH] of [MATH] cases, with a mean gain of [MATH] over those wins. We also propose an RLIM-tailored training mask for compact SBRNN detectors, improving the unmasked RLIM-SBRNN in [MATH] of [MATH] comparisons with [MATH] mean gain when masking is beneficial. Finally, the compact masked RLIM-SBRNN is competitive with channel-state-aware MLSE despite using no channel knowledge.
tldr: This paper proposes a masked neural detection method for constrained channel coding in molecular communication, focusing on run-length-limited ISI-mitigation codes.
motivation: Molecular communication suffers from severe diffusion memory, and neural detectors can outperform threshold detectors, raising the question of whether code advantages persist under neural detection.
method: The authors evaluate RLIM codes with sliding bidirectional recurrent neural network (SBRNN) detectors and propose an RLIM-tailored training mask for compact SBRNN detectors.
result: The best RLIM-SBRNN receiver beats the best uncoded receiver in most cases, and the masked detector improves performance further while remaining competitive with channel-state-aware MLSE.
conclusion: RLIM codes combined with neural detection provide significant BER gains in molecular communication, and the proposed masking technique enhances compact detector performance.

title: Compression Covariance And Tangent Kernels
authors: James Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be self-adjoint on a Hilbert space [MATH], let [MATH], and let [MATH] be an orthogonal projection. Relative to the decomposition [MATH], write \[ T_{t}=C_{t} & V^{*}_{t}\\ V_{t} & D_{t} , \] where [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. The compressed family [MATH] consists of positive contractions but need not form a semigroup. Its defect is given by \[ C_{s+t}-C_{s}C_{t}=V^{*}_{s}V_{t} \] while the complementary block satisfies \[ D_{s+t}-D_{s}D_{t}=V_{s}V^{*}_{t}. \] Thus the failure of [MATH] and [MATH] to be semigroups gives two Gram kernels associated with the same off-diagonal maps. tldr: The paper studies compression of self-adjoint operators and the resulting covariance defects as positive definite kernels, with a focus on tangent kernels and their Kolmogorov spaces.
motivation: To understand the hidden dynamics encoded in the defect of compressed operator families and to characterize short-time scaling limits.
method: Uses operator theory and Kolmogorov space formalism to analyze the covariance defects as Gram kernels and derive tangent kernels via rescaling.
result: The tangent kernel induces a positive self-adjoint contraction semigroup, and the representing vectors satisfy an additive cocycle identity.
conclusion: The work provides intrinsic restrictions on positive kernels that can arise as short-time compression covariance tangents.

title: The Capacity Region For Classes Of Sum-Broadcast Channels
authors: Amin Gohari, Yi Liu, Chandra Nair
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the capacity region of a sum of broadcast channels whose components are degraded, less-noisy, more-capable, deterministic, or semi-deterministic. We achieve this by showing that an auxiliary-receiver outer bound, previously introduced by some of the authors, matches Marton's inner bound. This result generalizes a previously known result for the sum of two reversely degraded broadcast channels due to El Gamal (1980). Moreover, we define a class of primary broadcast channels and show an analogous result for the sum of primary broadcast channels.
tldr: The paper computes the capacity region for sums of broadcast channels with certain properties, extending classical information theory results.
motivation: To characterize the capacity region of sum-broadcast channels, which are a type of multi-user channel, by showing that an outer bound matches Marton's inner bound.
method: The authors prove that an auxiliary-receiver outer bound coincides with Marton's inner bound for classes of degraded, less-noisy, more-capable, deterministic, and semi-deterministic broadcast channels.
result: The capacity region is fully characterized for these classes, generalizing El Gamal's result for two reversely degraded broadcast channels.
conclusion: The work provides a complete capacity characterization for sum-broadcast channels under the considered conditions, contributing to classical multi-user information theory.

title: Jscgc: Joint Source-Channel-Generation Coding For Wireless Generative Communications
authors: Tong Wu, Zhiyong Chen, Guo Lu, Li Song, Feng Yang, Meixia Tao, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional communication systems, including both separation-based coding and learning-based joint source-channel coding (JSCC), are typically designed under Shannon's rate-distortion theory. However, relying on generic distortion metrics fails to capture complex human visual perception, often resulting in blurred or unrealistic reconstructions. In this paper, we propose Joint Source-Channel-Generation Coding (JSCGC), a generative communication paradigm that replaces the conventional decoder with a generative model at the receiver. The received signal is treated as a condition that controls the sampling process into the learned conditional distribution, reformulating communication from deterministic reconstruction for distortion minimization to controlled generation for mutual information maximization under perceptual constraints. Based on this formulation, we develop a unified joint training and efficient stochastic sampling framework, and provide theoretical analysis of its effectiveness in both learning and inference stages. Extensive experiments on latent-space image transmission demonstrate that the JSCGC consistently improves feature-based, semantic-level, and distributional quality across diverse channel conditions, while exhibiting a distinct error behavior characterized by semantic inconsistency rather than distortion.
tldr: Proposes a joint source-channel-generation coding (JSCGC) paradigm for wireless image transmission using generative models at the receiver.
motivation: Conventional communication systems rely on distortion metrics that fail to capture human visual perception, leading to blurred or unrealistic reconstructions.
method: Replaces the conventional decoder with a generative model that treats the received signal as a condition for sampling from a learned conditional distribution, reformulating communication as controlled generation for mutual information maximization.
result: Experiments on latent-space image transmission show improved feature-based, semantic-level, and distributional quality across diverse channel conditions, with error behavior characterized by semantic inconsistency rather than distortion.
conclusion: JSCGC offers a new generative communication paradigm that enhances perceptual quality and semantic fidelity in wireless image transmission.

title: Randomized Optimal Switching Problem And Related Mirror Descent Flow
authors: Yuchao Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time reinforcement learning for the optimal switching problem, in which a decision-maker controls a diffusion process by switching among finitely many regimes, incurring both running and transition costs. To enable exploration, we relax the classical deterministic switching control to a randomized framework, where the switching decisions are governed by a continuous-time Markov chain with state-dependent generator, and augment the cost functional with a KL-divergence regularization weighted by a temperature parameter [MATH]. Under mild assumptions on the coefficients, we establish that the regularized value function is the unique smooth solution of an elliptic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman system, and derive an explicit optimal Gibbs policy given by an exponential transformation of the value function differences across modes. We further prove that the regularized value function approximates the classical optimal value function with error of order [MATH], which is consistent with analogous bounds established in other entropy-regularized control problems and is believed to be sharp. To solve the regularized problem numerically, we introduce a mirror descent flow in the dual logarithmic policy space, prove its well-posedness and the monotonic decrease of the value function along the flow, and establish quantitative error bound to the classical optimal value function. For a constant temperature scheduler, the convergence rate is of order [MATH], while under the annealing scheduler [MATH], we obtain the rate [MATH], which decays to zero as the flow time [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies a randomized optimal switching problem in continuous-time reinforcement learning using mirror descent flow.
motivation: The authors aim to solve optimal switching control problems with exploration by introducing randomization and entropy regularization.
method: They relax deterministic switching to a continuous-time Markov chain with KL-divergence regularization, derive the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system, and propose a mirror descent flow in the dual logarithmic policy space.
result: They prove the regularized value function is smooth, derive an explicit optimal Gibbs policy, and establish convergence rates for the mirror descent flow under constant and annealing temperature schedulers.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical and numerical framework for randomized optimal switching, with error bounds and convergence guarantees.

title: Bounds And Constructions Of Maximum Toroidal Distance Codes
authors: Pengjie Zhong, Jinquan Luo, Yufeng Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In lattice-based cryptographic schemes, both encoded messages and accumulated decryption noise are represented in a modulo [MATH] space. Therefore, it is natural to study toroidal distances and maximum toroidal distance (MTD) codes. In this paper, we derive some upper bounds for minimum toroidal distance of a code, including a Plotkin-type bound, a local ball--Plotkin bound, and a Delsarte linear programming bound. We also exhibit examples showing that these bounds are sharp in some cases. Moreover, we present several code constructions with good minimum distance, some of which are MTD codes. For [MATH], we obtain a family of four-point MTD codes in [MATH]. For [MATH], we propose a general code construction and exhibit several explicit instances for specific values of [MATH], some of which are proven to be MTD codes. For [MATH], using the [MATH] lattice, we construct codes [MATH], where [MATH] and show that they are MTD codes. These results give explicit optimal constructions of MTD codes for [MATH]. In the case [MATH], we construct a code with minimum toroidal distance [MATH] for [MATH], while the known upper bound in this case is [MATH]. Our main tools are geometric and linear programming methods.
tldr: This paper studies maximum toroidal distance codes, which are relevant to lattice-based cryptography, but not to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: Toroidal distance codes are used in lattice-based cryptographic schemes to represent encoded messages and decryption noise, motivating the need for optimal code constructions.
method: The authors derive upper bounds (Plotkin-type, local ball-Plotkin, Delsarte linear programming) and provide explicit code constructions using geometric and linear programming methods.
result: They obtain optimal MTD codes for various parameters, including a family of four-point MTD codes in Z_2^2 and constructions using the A_2 lattice for n=3.
conclusion: The work provides explicit optimal constructions and sharp bounds for toroidal distance codes, advancing coding theory for lattice-based cryptography.

title: A Quadratic Order Reduction -- Gaussian Process Ordinary Differential Equation Framework For The Inference Of Large Continuous Dynamical Systems
authors: Guglielmo Padula, Michele Girfoglio, Gianluigi Rozza
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecasting the evolution of complex dynamical systems remains a fundamentally challenging task, primarily due to pronounced nonlinear interactions, high-dimensional state spaces, and the concomitant requirement for rigorous and reliable uncertainty quantification. Contemporary reduced-order modelling (ROM) frameworks frequently exhibit inherent trade-offs among predictive accuracy, numerical stability, and interpretability, and thus often fail to achieve an optimal balance among these competing objectives. To address these limitations, we propose a framework for forecasting complex dynamical systems via a kernel autonomous ordinary differential equation approach based on Gaussian Processes and Quadratic Order Model Reduction. Our base method, the Gaussian Process Ordinary Differential Equations model, allows accurate short-term forecasting with uncertainty quantification, and it provably converges to the real autonomous equation in the smooth case. We integrate it with quadratic order reduced-order modelling and sphere projection for learning the latent dynamics efficiently while preserving stability. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our full model outperforms ROM forecasting methods such as Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition, Bagging Optimised Dynamic Mode Decomposition and Linear and Nonlinear Disambiguation Optimisation in terms of accuracy or computational costs. These results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a robust and stable tool for forecasting complex dynamical systems with rigorous uncertainty quantification.
tldr: A machine learning framework combining Gaussian processes and quadratic order reduction for forecasting large dynamical systems.
motivation: Existing reduced-order models for complex dynamical systems often trade off accuracy, stability, and interpretability.
method: The framework integrates Gaussian Process Ordinary Differential Equations with quadratic order model reduction and sphere projection to learn latent dynamics efficiently.
result: The proposed method outperforms several dynamic mode decomposition variants in accuracy and computational cost on numerical experiments.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust tool for forecasting complex dynamical systems with uncertainty quantification.

title: Consistency Of Variational Approximations Under Bounded Kullback--Leibler Divergence
authors: Hien Duy Nguyen, Jacob Westerhout, Thomas Guilmeau, Julyan Arbel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational methods are widely used to approximate posterior distributions in Bayesian inference when exact computation is infeasible. We study when such approximations inherit posterior consistency. Our first result shows that, on a general metric space, a uniform bound on the Kullback--Leibler divergence from the approximating measures to a tight sequence of target measures forces the approximating sequence to be tight. It follows that if the target posteriors converge weakly to a Dirac mass at the true parameter, then any variational sequence with bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence to the targets is also consistent. We also give simple logarithmic-moment conditions that verify this boundedness condition, and illustrate them for smooth generalised posterior distributions.
tldr: This paper proves that variational approximations with bounded KL divergence to a consistent posterior sequence are themselves consistent, using tightness and logarithmic-moment conditions.
motivation: Variational inference is widely used but its theoretical guarantees, especially posterior consistency, are not well understood. The authors aim to provide general conditions under which variational approximations inherit consistency.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments: they show that uniform boundedness of KL divergence from approximating measures to a tight sequence of target measures implies tightness of the approximating sequence. They then derive logarithmic-moment conditions to verify boundedness.
result: If the target posteriors converge weakly to a Dirac mass at the true parameter, any variational sequence with bounded KL divergence to the targets is also consistent. Simple logarithmic-moment conditions are given and illustrated for smooth generalized posteriors.
conclusion: Variational approximations can be consistent under mild conditions, providing theoretical justification for their use in Bayesian inference.

title: Auto Formalisation Of Chaitin And Of The Surprise Incompleteness Theorem
authors: Thierry Coquand
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a continuation of a previous report on an experiment in autoformalisation of G\"odel's second incompleteness theorem in Agda using Claude. Using the framework built in this experiment, Claude could ``automformalise'' Chaitin's proof of the first incompleteness theorem and then the Kritchman-Raz surprise examination paradox version of the second incompleteness. As the first experiment, the project provides a case study of the strengths and limitations of current large language models in mathematics. Since Chaitin's proof involves coding programs, Claude had to represent code as ternary string and could build autonomously a parser and a continuation stack evaluation machine. The fact that we can simulate computations as expected is not completely trivial and we suggested a Gandy/Howard majorisation argument, that Claude had no problem to follow. The resulting formalisation clarifies a number of details left implicit in the original presentation and provides a fully machine-checked proof of these arguments for Church's Basic Recursive Arithmetic.
tldr: This paper reports on an experiment in autoformalising Chaitin's incompleteness theorem and the surprise examination paradox in Agda using Claude, focusing on the capabilities of large language models in mathematics.
motivation: To explore the strengths and limitations of current LLMs in formalising mathematical proofs, specifically incompleteness theorems.
method: Using the Claude LLM to autoformalise proofs in Agda, building on a previous framework for Gödel's second incompleteness theorem.
result: Claude successfully autoformalised Chaitin's proof and the Kritchman-Raz surprise examination paradox, including autonomous construction of a parser and evaluation machine.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates that LLMs can assist in formalising non-trivial mathematical arguments, but also highlights limitations and the need for human guidance.

title: Modern Analog Computing For Solving Differential And Matrix Equations
authors: Zhong Sun, Piergiulio Mannocci, Manuel Le Gallo, Abu Sebastian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, driven by the computational demands of data-intensive applications such as artificial intelligence and scientific computing, analog computing has gained renewed interest. Given the diversity of computational tasks and recent advancements in analog CMOS circuits and resistive memory technologies, we refer to the evolving landscape as modern analog computing. In this context, we identify three core computational primitives: solving differential equations, solving matrix equations, and performing matrix-vector multiplications, and we explore the connections among them. We also examine various hardware implementations of these analog computing operators, including those built with discrete components, integrated circuits, and resistive memory devices. Among these, resistive memory arrays emerge as particularly promising due to their implementation efficiency. The paper then surveys recent progress in leveraging modern analog computing to solve differential and matrix equations using both advanced analog CMOS circuits and resistive memory arrays. Finally, we discuss the applications of these circuits, the precision and scalability issues and their potential solutions, the relationship with in-memory computing, and the unique computational complexity of analog computing. This paper provides a unified perspective on analog computing, highlighting its strengths, current developments, and challenges, and positioning it as a pivotal enabler of next-generation computational frontiers.
tldr: A survey of modern analog computing for solving differential and matrix equations using CMOS circuits and resistive memory arrays.
motivation: To address the computational demands of data-intensive applications like AI and scientific computing by reviving analog computing.
method: Identifies three core primitives (solving differential equations, matrix equations, matrix-vector multiplications) and reviews hardware implementations including discrete components, integrated circuits, and resistive memory arrays.
result: Resistive memory arrays are highlighted as particularly promising for efficient implementation; the paper surveys recent progress and discusses precision, scalability, and complexity issues.
conclusion: Modern analog computing, especially with resistive memory, is positioned as a key enabler for next-generation computing, but the paper does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Intent-Based Cryptographic Api Design For Cryptographic Agility
authors: Gregoire Messmer Navaneeth Rameshan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As organizations move toward post-quantum cryptography, they face the major challenge of updating cryptographic algorithms across large, complex software portfolios. However, most cryptographic APIs in use today were designed around specific algorithms. These APIs expect explicit use of specific algorithms, provide little or no support for policy-based algorithm selection, and offer no straightforward way to migrate existing keys to newer algorithms. This makes the transition to post-quantum cryptography challenging. The companion assessment framework identifies the barriers to cryptographic agility and explains why algorithm transition is largely a software engineering problem. To address the limitations of current cryptographic APIs, we identify the principles necessary to design a cryptographically agile API. The design principles are derived from five fundamental architectural characteristics (Abstraction, Stability, Temporal Flexibility, Separation, and Extensibility). We also show how the design principles can be implemented using several examples of Protocol Buffers API design patterns. In particular, we present an intent vocabulary that is based on scopes which allows for decoupling key creation from algorithm identities. It also supports transparent substitutions of algorithms in the applicable scope. Cryptographic governance is enabled by an abstract policy API that does not prescribe the policy format. Keys are represented by stable identifiers and support key evolution operations (rotation, transformation, migration), facilitating migration between algorithms and providers while tracking both the original key identity and its evolution history. With this approach, updating cryptography becomes an operational process without the need to rewrite application code.
tldr: This paper proposes design principles and an intent-based API for cryptographic agility to ease the transition to post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: Current cryptographic APIs are tightly coupled to specific algorithms, making it difficult to migrate to post-quantum cryptography across large software portfolios.
method: The authors identify five architectural characteristics (Abstraction, Stability, Temporal Flexibility, Separation, Extensibility) and implement them using Protocol Buffers API design patterns, including an intent vocabulary and abstract policy API.
result: The proposed API design decouples key creation from algorithm identities, supports transparent algorithm substitution, and enables key evolution operations without rewriting application code.
conclusion: Updating cryptography becomes an operational process, facilitating the transition to post-quantum algorithms.

title: $W-\delta-\mu$ Dual Codes And Lcd Codes
authors: Satyadeep Pandey Avanish Kumar Chaturvedi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new product on the ambient space [MATH] as a generalization of Euclidean, Hermitian and [MATH] products. We give some general properties of the dual codes, relation with Euclidean duals, definition and characterization of self orthogonal, self dual, dual containing and LCD codes along with certain existence conditions. Also, we calculate the dual codes of some classes of codes like repetition, binary and [MATH]-constacyclic codes with respect to this product. Further, we extend and analyse this notion of the product for codes over semisimple rings.
tldr: This paper introduces a new product on ambient spaces to generalize Euclidean, Hermitian, and other products, and studies dual codes, self-orthogonal, self-dual, dual-containing, and LCD codes over finite fields and semisimple rings.
motivation: To unify and extend the theory of dual codes and LCD codes under a generalized product, providing existence conditions and characterizations.
method: Defines a new product (W-δ-μ) on the ambient space, derives properties of dual codes, and computes duals for specific code families like repetition and constacyclic codes.
result: Establishes general properties of dual codes under the new product, characterizes self-orthogonal and LCD codes, and gives explicit dual code calculations for several code classes.
conclusion: The new product framework offers a unified approach to study dual codes and LCD codes, with potential applications in coding theory.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Hypergraph Edge Partitioning Under Independent Edge Sampling
authors: Javad Maheri, K. K. Krishnan Namboodiri, Petros Elia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hypergraph edge partitioning is a central problem in theoretical and applied computer science, with broad impact on distributed computation, communications, optimization, and machine learning. In this setting, one is given a collection of hyperedges -- each consisting of up to [MATH] vertices from a ground set of size [MATH] -- and seeks to assign these hyperedges across [MATH] partitions so as to minimize, for example, the vertex footprint, i.e., the maximum number of vertices that appear in any partition. We here identify the fundamental limits of hypergraph edge partitioning -- optimized over all conceivable algorithms -- for a broad class of probabilistic hypergraph models where each hyperedge may appear independently with probability; a model sufficiently general to encompass well-known models such as the Degree-Corrected or Mixed-Membership models, the Hypergraph Stochastic Block model, the Latent-Space/Geometric or Kernel Models, and others. By pairing our deterministic partitioner with a new converse, we first show that, for any [MATH], and under the very mild condition of [MATH], as long as the hyperedge set [MATH] satisfies [MATH], then with probability at least [MATH], no algorithm can provide a footprint [MATH] less than $[MATH][MATH]\pi^{\bigstar}_{}[MATH][MATH]n$), and it additionally entails a near-optimally balanced allocation of hyperedges across partitions.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on hypergraph edge partitioning under independent edge sampling, focusing on minimizing vertex footprint across partitions.
motivation: Hypergraph edge partitioning is important for distributed computation and machine learning, but fundamental limits were unknown for probabilistic hypergraph models.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the vertex footprint using a converse argument and pair it with a deterministic partitioner to show near-optimality.
result: For a broad class of probabilistic hypergraph models, any algorithm must have a vertex footprint at least a certain fraction of the total vertices, with high probability.
conclusion: The work provides tight fundamental limits and a near-optimal algorithm for hypergraph edge partitioning under independent edge sampling.

title: Omnidirectional Photonic Chiral Flatband In Nonlocal Membrane Metasurfaces
authors: Baohe Zhang, Jumin Qiu, Meng Qin, Haiyan Jiang, Shuyuan Xiao, Zhiwei Zheng, Leman Kuang, Hui Jing, Xinxing Zhou, Hongju Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Omnidirectional flat-band resonances, characterized by an enhanced photonic density of states and inherent angular robustness, are highly sought-after in integrated nanophotonic devices, particularly when integrated with chiral functionality. Here we realize such resonances in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air-hole arrays. Increasing the lattice period not only compresses the Brillouin zone but, crucially, weakens the evanescent coupling between neighbouring Bloch modes associated with the same-order guided resonances. Driven by the tight-binding model in the limit of weak inter-unit-cell coupling, the pronounced band flattening of the degenerate guided resonance along both [MATH] and [MATH] yields, giving rise to an omnidirectional flat-band resonance. Remarkably, both numerical simulations and experiments reveal a universal route for endowing flat-band guided resonances with optical chirality through the deliberate breaking of the mirror symmetry of air holes. As a result, the omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance emerges along both principal in-plane directions, with [MATH]-factors exceeding 10[MATH] and circular dichroism greater than 0.9 over a wide angular range of [MATH]. Nonlinear measurements further show that the resulting resonance not only drives highly efficient third-harmonic generation but also imparts a pronounced spin-selective character to the nonlinear process. Simultaneously, the highly efficient nonlinear process also enables chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a general paradigm for engineering omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonances in planar silicon platforms, opening new opportunities for nonlinear nanophotonics and chiral imaging.
tldr: This paper demonstrates omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonances in nonlocal silicon membrane metasurfaces for nonlinear nanophotonics and chiral imaging.
motivation: To achieve omnidirectional flat-band resonances with chiral functionality for integrated nanophotonic devices.
method: The authors use a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface with periodic square-lattice air-hole arrays, breaking mirror symmetry to induce chirality, and employ tight-binding modeling and experiments.
result: They observe flat-band resonances with Q-factors >10^4 and circular dichroism >0.9 over a wide angular range, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation and chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging.
conclusion: This work establishes a general paradigm for engineering omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonances in planar silicon platforms, opening opportunities for nonlinear nanophotonics and chiral imaging.

title: Design And Optimization Of An AZO-based Plasmonic Metasurface-driven Optical Solar Reflector For Thermal Management
authors: Lucas Viseur, Alexandre Mayer, Luc Henrard, Micha\"el Lobet
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plasmonic metasurface-driven Optical Solar Reflectors (m-OSRs) offer a promising route towards lightweight and high-performance thermal management. By exploiting subwavelength structuring and intrinsic material losses, such systems enable tailored absorptance spectrum across the solar and thermal infrared domains, respectively. Here, a plasmonic m-OSR composed of an aluminum back-reflector, a silicon dioxide dielectric spacer, and a nanostructured aluminum-doped zinc oxide (AZO) layer is investigated. The optical response of the structure is governed by the interplay between reflection, localized surface plasmon resonances and Fabry-Perot cavity effects, leading to efficient spectral selectivity. An optimization performed with a multi-objective genetic algorithm yields a low solar absorptance of alpha = 0.16 combined with a high thermal emissivity of epsilon = 0.83, providing an alpha/epsilon ratio of 0.19. These results highlight the potential of plasmonic meta-OSRs as ultrathin, high-performance solutions for thermal management and in particular for the next-generation advanced spacecraft.
tldr: This paper designs and optimizes an AZO-based plasmonic metasurface for thermal management in spacecraft, achieving low solar absorptance and high thermal emissivity.
motivation: Lightweight and efficient thermal management is critical for spacecraft, and traditional Optical Solar Reflectors (OSRs) are heavy. Plasmonic metasurfaces offer a promising alternative.
method: The authors simulate a multilayer structure (Al back-reflector, SiO2 spacer, nanostructured AZO) and use a multi-objective genetic algorithm to optimize the geometry for low solar absorptance and high thermal emissivity.
result: The optimized design achieves a solar absorptance of 0.16 and thermal emissivity of 0.83, yielding an alpha/epsilon ratio of 0.19.
conclusion: Plasmonic metasurface OSRs are ultrathin, high-performance solutions for spacecraft thermal management.

title: Exploring Fair Access To Quantum Computing
authors: Pieter Vermaas Benedict Lane
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This short article - commissioned as part of the Quantum Flagship project OpenSuperQPlus - introduces the topic of fair access to quantum computing time and argues for its relevance in current European technology policy debates. Choices about access we make today affect which applications of quantum computing are developed in the future, and by whom. Among the issues at stake are: Europe's technological autonomy and sovereignty; Europe's future economic competitiveness; knowledge security and the future of open science; and delivering upon the EU's founding values and aims. The results of a survey of OpenSuperQPlus researchers reveal prevalent contractualist and transactional framings of access to European quantum computing capacity among those developing the technology. The article concludes with a call to go beyond framing access to quantum computing as a zero-sum-game, and to explore the possibility of an access regime premised on openness and solidarity.
tldr: This paper discusses policy and ethical issues around fair access to quantum computing, not technical quantum research.
motivation: To argue for fair access to quantum computing resources in European policy debates.
method: Conceptual analysis and survey of researchers.
result: Identifies prevalent contractualist and transactional framings among researchers.
conclusion: Calls for an access regime based on openness and solidarity.

title: A Lattice-theoretic Framework For Hesitant Fuzzy Convexity Beyond Scalar Observables
authors: Carlos Salvatierra, Pedro Huidobro, Raquel Fernandez-Peralta
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In fuzzy-set theory, the notion of convexity has often been formulated through scalar reductions, typically via scores and aggregation functions. Although useful, such reductions may obscure relevant order-theoretic information in the codomain, especially in complex set-valued settings. This article develops a lattice-theoretic framework for convexity on lattice-valued mappings over point-convex segment-generated abstract convexity spaces. The framework separates the segment structure of the domain from the lattice structure of the codomain, distinguishing intrinsic convexity, defined through the lattice meet, from relational and observable convexities induced by preorders or scalar maps. The article characterizes when scalar observables preserve or reconstruct intrinsic convexity, and which codomain operators preserve it through their pointwise extensions. It then specializes the framework to hesitant fuzzy sets endowed with the symmetric lattice, recovering classical fuzzy and interval-valued convexities as natural restrictions. The structural result shows that the symmetric order cannot be represented by any finite family of scalar observables. This obstruction appears even on two-point typical hesitant fuzzy elements. Consequently, symmetric hesitant convexity cannot, in general, be reconstructed by any finite family of scalar observables. Moreover, every finite family of monotone scalar observables admits a three-point hesitant profile that is scalar-convex for all selected descriptions but not symmetrically convex.
tldr: This paper develops a lattice-theoretic framework for convexity in hesitant fuzzy sets, focusing on order-theoretic properties and the limitations of scalar observables.
motivation: Traditional scalar-based reductions of convexity in fuzzy set theory may lose order-theoretic information, especially in complex set-valued settings like hesitant fuzzy sets.
method: The authors separate the segment structure of the domain from the lattice structure of the codomain, defining intrinsic, relational, and observable convexities, and analyze when scalar observables preserve or reconstruct intrinsic convexity.
result: The symmetric order in hesitant fuzzy sets cannot be represented by any finite family of scalar observables, even on two-point elements, and there exist profiles that are scalar-convex but not symmetrically convex.
conclusion: The framework reveals fundamental limitations of scalar-based approaches to convexity in hesitant fuzzy sets, suggesting that richer lattice-theoretic methods are necessary.

title: The Dyadic Cauchy-Kernel Identity: Several Roads Back To Classical Objects
authors: Nicholas Castillo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is an expository note. We take the dyadic Cauchy-kernel identity of Castillo-Costin-Costin, a global rational/factorial decomposition built on the polylogarithm, and follow it down several specializations.
