In each direction it returns to a classical landmark: the polylogarithm duplication formula and Hurwitz's Fourier-series formula; representations of the zeta function at the special argument pi and at rational arguments, in the neighborhood of Hurwitz's multiplication theorem; the Hasse-Sondow globally convergent series; and, through its discrete scale invariance, the extra zeros of the Dirichlet eta function together with the harmonic-sum asymptotics of Flajolet-Gourdon-Dumas, with Dirichlet L-values emerging as the amplitudes of a log-periodic oscillation. The aim is unification: to exhibit one compact identity as an organizing center from which these classical results may be read off. We claim no new theorems; where an identity may not previously have been displayed in exactly this form, we say so and explain why it is nonetheless a recombination of known ingredients.
tldr: An expository note showing how the dyadic Cauchy-kernel identity unifies several classical results in number theory and special functions.
motivation: To demonstrate that a single rational/factorial decomposition can serve as an organizing center for diverse classical identities.
method: The paper specializes the dyadic Cauchy-kernel identity to derive known formulas for polylogarithms, zeta functions, and Dirichlet L-values.
result: The identity reproduces the polylogarithm duplication formula, Hurwitz's Fourier-series formula, Hasse-Sondow series, and extra zeros of the Dirichlet eta function.
conclusion: The identity provides a unifying perspective but claims no new theorems; it is a recombination of known ingredients.

title: Structure-preserving Discretization And Fingering Dynamics Of A Cahn-Hilliard Model For Traction-driven Digit Morphogenesis
authors: Marvin Fritz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Cahn-Hilliard equation with anisotropic traction flux arising as a reduced continuum model of mechanically biased cell interactions in digit-forming organoids. For a regularized problem with strictly positive bounded mobility, we introduce a mixed finite element discretization based on an implicit-explicit treatment of the chemical potential. We prove existence of discrete solutions, establish exact mass conservation and a discrete energy inequality, and show convergence of the fully discrete approximations to a weak solution of the regularized problem. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting dynamics and show the transition from classical coarsening to traction-induced fingering and protrusive growth. The computational study is complemented by mass and energy diagnostics, an energy-balance residual, fingering-onset and protrusion-count diagnostics, and a manufactured-solution convergence study.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical analysis of a Cahn-Hilliard model for digit morphogenesis, focusing on structure-preserving discretization and fingering dynamics.
motivation: Understanding digit formation in organoids requires modeling cell interactions with mechanical bias, which this reduced continuum model aims to capture.
method: A mixed finite element discretization with implicit-explicit treatment of chemical potential is introduced, and convergence to weak solutions is proved.
result: Numerical experiments show transition from classical coarsening to traction-induced fingering and protrusive growth, with mass and energy diagnostics.
conclusion: The proposed discretization preserves mass and energy properties, and the model captures key morphogenetic dynamics.

title: On $m$-partial Isometries: Spectra, Weighted Shifts, And Similarity
authors: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui, Micha{\l} Bucha{\l}a, Stephan Ramon Garcia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to study [MATH]-partial isometries on Hilbert spaces, a natural extension of partial isometries and [MATH]-isometries. We establish structural and spectral results, characterize the [MATH]-partial isometric weighted shifts, and investigate similarity to [MATH]-isometries and [MATH]-partial isometries.
tldr: This paper studies m-partial isometries on Hilbert spaces, a purely mathematical topic with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To extend the theory of partial isometries and m-isometries to m-partial isometries, establishing structural and spectral results.
method: Functional analysis and operator theory techniques, including spectral analysis and characterization of weighted shifts.
result: Characterization of m-partial isometric weighted shifts and similarity conditions to m-isometries and m-partial isometries.
conclusion: The work contributes to operator theory but has no application to the user's research interests.

title: Characterizing Metric-space-valued Processes: Separating Classes And Weak Invariance Principles For Measure-theoretic Inference
authors: Anne van Delft
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article investigates stochastic processes taking values in metric spaces that lack a topological vector space structure, a regime characterized by intricate interplay between topological, geometric, and temporal dependence structures. It is formally established that spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding constitute a strict subclass within the much broader class of metric spaces possessing the ball property. While traditional kernel methods are susceptible to geometric distortion when the underlying space cannot be isometrically embedded into a Hilbert space, we bypass such limitations by exploiting a fundamental structural property inherent to this broader class; namely, that Borel probability measures are uniquely determined by their values on balls. These separating classes provide the foundation for the subsequently introduced measure-theoretic inference methodology. We derive uniform convergence of a family of time-dependent random measures, alongside weak invariance principles for the corresponding nonstationary random fields. This framework explicitly exposes how dependence and geometric complexity influence sample path regularity. Furthermore, because the rapid decay of small-ball probabilities can prohibit the existence of limiting distributions for supremum-based discrepancy measures, we develop [MATH]-based alternatives. By directly leveraging the introduced convergence results, this approach circumvents the need for higher-order [MATH]-process formulations. Finally, for spaces that do admit an isometric Hilbertian embedding, and where [MATH]-processes naturally arise, we establish limit theory for both degenerate and nondegenerate multi-parameter [MATH]-processes, and demonstrate that local discrepancy tests maintain asymptotic stability under dynamic parameter regimes.
tldr: This paper develops measure-theoretic inference for stochastic processes on metric spaces without vector space structure, focusing on separating classes and weak invariance principles.
motivation: Traditional kernel methods fail when the metric space cannot be isometrically embedded into a Hilbert space, motivating a new approach based on the ball property.
method: The authors exploit that Borel probability measures on such spaces are uniquely determined by their values on balls, and derive uniform convergence of time-dependent random measures and weak invariance principles.
result: They establish that spaces with isometric Hilbertian embedding are a strict subclass of those with the ball property, and develop U-process-based alternatives to supremum-based discrepancy measures.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust methodology for inference on metric-space-valued processes, with asymptotic stability under dynamic parameter regimes.

title: Twist Deformations For Hopf Coquasigroups
authors: Brais Ramos P\'erez Ram\'on Gonz\'alez Rodr\'iguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a general theory of twist deformations for Hopf coquasigroups in a symmetric monoidal category. To this end, we first introduce and study non-coassociative bimonoids endowed with left and right codivisions, and establish their connection with left and right Hopf coquasigroups. Next, motivated by the classical theory of Drinfeld twists for Hopf algebras, we define twists for non-coassociative bimonoids and prove that they induce deformations of Hopf coquasigroup structures through suitable modifications of the coproduct. In particular, we obtain explicit deformation procedures for right and left Hopf coquasigroups and analyze the corresponding antipodes. Finally, we apply the general theory to construct nontrivial examples arising from Hopf coquasigroups associated with the sphere [MATH], obtaining new examples of twisted Hopf coquasigroups that are neither commutative nor cocommutative.
tldr: Develops a theory of twist deformations for Hopf coquasigroups in symmetric monoidal categories, generalizing Drinfeld twists to non-coassociative settings.
motivation: To extend the classical theory of Drinfeld twists for Hopf algebras to Hopf coquasigroups, which are non-coassociative structures, and to construct new examples.
method: Introduces non-coassociative bimonoids with left and right codivisions, defines twists for them, and proves that twists induce deformations of Hopf coquasigroup structures via modified coproducts.
result: Obtains explicit deformation procedures for right and left Hopf coquasigroups and constructs nontrivial twisted examples from Hopf coquasigroups associated with the sphere.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for twist deformations in non-coassociative settings, yielding new non-commutative, non-cocommutative Hopf coquasigroups.

title: From Parameters To Feature Space: Task Arithmetic For Backdoor Mitigation In Model Merging
authors: Zhenqian Zhu, Yamin Hu, Yiya Diao, Weixiang Li, Haodong Li, Wenjian Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging (MM) has gained significant attention as a cost-effective approach to integrate multiple task-specific models into a unified model. However, recent work reveals that MM is highly susceptible to backdoor attacks. Existing defenses based on task arithmetic often fail to eliminate backdoors without substantially degrading clean-task performance, owing to their reliance on direct parameter-space editing. To address this gap, we propose Linear Feature Path Minimization (LFPM), a backdoor mitigation framework for model merging, which introduces an anti-backdoor task vector into the backdoored merged model. Unlike prior approaches, LFPM formulates the backdoor robustness of the merged model from a unified feature-space perspective under the Cross-Task Linearity (CTL) framework, which leverages the approximate linearity of features across tasks. This perspective guides the optimization of the anti-backdoor task to suppress backdoors while preserving clean-task performance. Furthermore, we introduce an effective optimization mechanism based on gradient accumulation and loss path-integral, ensuring robust backdoor suppression along the interpolation path. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LFPM consistently exhibits strong robustness against backdoor attacks in both full fine-tuning and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) settings.
tldr: This paper proposes a backdoor mitigation framework for model merging in machine learning, using feature-space linearity to suppress backdoors while preserving clean-task performance.
motivation: Model merging is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and existing parameter-space defenses degrade clean-task performance.
method: The authors introduce Linear Feature Path Minimization (LFPM), which optimizes an anti-backdoor task vector under the Cross-Task Linearity (CTL) framework using gradient accumulation and loss path-integral.
result: LFPM consistently shows strong robustness against backdoor attacks in both full fine-tuning and PEFT settings.
conclusion: Feature-space approaches can effectively mitigate backdoors in model merging without sacrificing clean-task accuracy.

title: The Switching Lemma Shows What The Switching Lemma Cannot Prove: An Unconditional Natural-proofs Barrier
authors: Bruno Loff, Suhail Sherif, Navid Talebanfard, Francesca Ugazio
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Razborov and Rudich (JCSS'97) observed that all known lower-bound proofs follow a certain pattern: when showing that a function [MATH] is hard, along the way the proof provides us with a distinguisher, namely, an efficient algorithm which can distinguish easy functions from random functions. They called such lower-bound proofs natural proofs. They then showed a natural-proofs barrier: under standard cryptographic assumptions, natural proofs cannot show superpolynomial lower-bounds against Boolean circuits. Along similar lines it can be shown that under a suitable cryptographic assumption, natural proofs cannot significantly improve the current state-of-the-art lower bound against constant depth circuits (AC0). The state of the art, using Hstad's Switching Lemma (SL), is [MATH] for depth-[MATH] circuits, and (conditionally) no natural proof can prove lower bounds of [MATH] for some large constant [MATH]. In this paper we revisit the natural-proofs barrier from an [MATH] perspective. We focus on AC0-natural proofs, i.e. proofs whose distinguishers are computable by AC0 circuits. Razborov and Rudich observed that lower bounds based on SL are AC0-natural. We show that this is true for most known lower-bound techniques against constant-depth circuits. We then establish an unconditional barrier for such proofs. By localizing the Trevisan--Xue pseudorandom generator, we are able to show that no AC0-natural proof can prove a lower bound greater than [MATH] against depth-[MATH] circuits. This is in the same quantitative regime as the SL frontier which instead has [MATH] in the power of [MATH]. The proof has a striking self-referential aspect: the proof of security of the Trevisan--Xue generator crucially relies on SL, and so SL has been used to show that AC0-natural proofs, such as SL itself, cannot prove AC0 lower bounds better than that of SL.
tldr: This paper proves an unconditional barrier for AC0-natural proofs, showing that such proofs cannot improve AC0 lower bounds beyond a certain threshold, using a self-referential argument that relies on the Switching Lemma itself.
motivation: To understand the limitations of natural proofs in complexity theory, specifically for constant-depth circuits, and to establish an unconditional barrier that does not rely on cryptographic assumptions.
method: The authors localize the Trevisan–Xue pseudorandom generator and use the Switching Lemma to prove that no AC0-natural proof can prove a lower bound greater than n^{log^{O(1)} n} against depth-d circuits.
result: They show that AC0-natural proofs cannot prove lower bounds beyond n^{log^{O(1)} n}, which is in the same regime as the current state-of-the-art from the Switching Lemma.
conclusion: The Switching Lemma itself cannot be used to prove significantly better AC0 lower bounds via natural proofs, establishing an unconditional barrier for such proof techniques.

title: An Assessment Framework For Application-Level Cryptographic Agility
authors: Gregoire Messmer Navaneeth Rameshan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The impending post-quantum transition to new cryptography will require complete replacement of algorithms within all software. The cryptographic APIs used today make this transition challenging because they were not designed with agility as a concern. There is no method for systematically assessing cryptographic agility as an overall ability. In addition to this, the term itself refers to multiple independent capabilities. Specifically, it includes replacing algorithms, selecting by policy, and substituting implementations. This lack of structured decomposition limits both the evaluation of systems and the development of cryptographically agile APIs. We introduce a component-based assessment framework that characterizes application-level cryptographic agility along seven orthogonal dimensions: three coupling dimensions that measure what the application code knows about algorithms and providers, a cross-cutting decoupling mechanism, a governance authority dimension, and two agility enablers that measure actual migration capability. The framework is non-linear and captures non-hierarchical profiles: a system may achieve high operation decoupling yet low creation decoupling, or strong versioning without externalized configuration. We evaluate six representative APIs (PKCS#11, OpenSSL~3.0, JCA, Google Tink, AWS KMS, and HashiCorp Vault Transit) against the framework, revealing three pervasive and independent gaps: no system supports intent-based key creation, none provides policy-driven algorithm selection (as distinct from access control), and none offers dedicated/first-class operations for algorithm transformation of existing keys. These gaps are individually sufficient to prevent agile migration, explaining why the post-quantum transition remains a software engineering problem despite decades of API progress.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for assessing cryptographic agility in software APIs, focusing on the post-quantum transition.
motivation: Current cryptographic APIs lack systematic support for algorithm replacement, policy selection, and implementation substitution, hindering the post-quantum transition.
method: The authors define seven orthogonal dimensions for agility assessment and evaluate six representative APIs against this framework.
result: Three pervasive gaps are identified: no intent-based key creation, no policy-driven algorithm selection, and no dedicated operations for key transformation.
conclusion: The framework reveals that these gaps individually prevent agile migration, explaining why the post-quantum transition remains a software engineering challenge.

title: A Near-quadratic Lower Bound On The Border Determinantal Complexity Of $\sum_i X_i^n$ Via Conormal Specialization
authors: Karthik Sheshadri
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The border determinantal complexity [MATH] of a polynomial [MATH] is the least [MATH] such that [MATH] is a limit of determinants of [MATH] matrices of affine-linear forms. We prove that for every [MATH], over [MATH], \[ \dcb\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^n\Big)\ \ge\ {4e}, \qquad \sdcb\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^n\Big)\ \ge\ {2e} \] in the ordinary and symmetric models respectively; both match the known [MATH] upper bounds up to the constant. To our knowledge these are the first border determinantal lower bounds for an explicit family that are superlinear in the number of variables: the known quadratic border bound for the permanent reads the of the dual variety and is linear in its number of variables, whereas we transfer the dual . The proof has two ingredients. The first is an unconditional bound on the slot-[MATH] conormal multidegree of the multiplicity-one Gauss-graph cycle of an arbitrary affine-linear determinant -- singular, reducible, and non-reduced fibers allowed -- by a multihomogeneous B\'ezout count of a lifted kernel incidence. The second is a specialization argument: along any degeneration [MATH], the flat limit of these Gauss-graph cycles contains the conormal variety of the Fermat cone with positive coefficient. A cone-shift identity converts that conormal multidegree into the classical dual degree [MATH] of the smooth Fermat hypersurface, and an [MATH]-st root yields the quadratic bound. The exact lower bounds of the author's companion manuscripts follow as corollaries.
tldr: This paper proves near-quadratic lower bounds on the border determinantal complexity of the polynomial sum of n-th powers, using conormal specialization and dual variety techniques.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of polynomials is a central problem in algebraic complexity theory; border determinantal complexity measures the size of a determinantal representation needed to approximate a polynomial.
method: The proof combines an unconditional bound on the conormal multidegree of Gauss-graph cycles of affine-linear determinants with a specialization argument that relates the flat limit to the conormal variety of the Fermat cone, then uses a cone-shift identity to connect to the dual degree of the Fermat hypersurface.
result: Lower bounds of Ω(n^2) for ordinary border determinantal complexity and Ω(n^2) for symmetric border determinantal complexity are obtained, matching known upper bounds up to constants.
conclusion: These are the first superlinear border determinantal lower bounds for an explicit family, demonstrating the power of geometric methods in algebraic complexity.

title: Identifiability Without Gaussianity: Symbolic World Models And Near-Infinite Temporal Consistency
authors: {\l}ukasz Chmiel Seth Dobrin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Klindt, LeCun, and Balestriero (arXiv:2605.26379) proved that Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) achieve linear identifiability, the linear recovery of the world's true latent variables, if and only if the world's latent dynamics follow a Gaussian, stationary process. This Gaussian boundary implies a fundamental limit on temporal consistency: for any non-Gaussian physical system, the representation error of a statistical World Model grows monotonically with time. We prove that this limit is an artifact of the statistical alignment mechanism, not a property of World Models in general. We introduce the Physics-Grounded Symbolic Architecture (PGSA) and prove three results: (1) a PGSA achieves exact linear identifiability for all physical regimes, regardless of the latent distribution; (2) the per-step error of a PGSA is bounded by numerical precision alone; and (3) as a direct consequence, a PGSA maintains temporal consistency for an unbounded number of transitions, a property we term near-infinite temporal consistency. We further prove that statistical World Models cannot achieve this property for any non-Gaussian system, regardless of model capacity or the volume of training data. The algebraic cores of four of the theorems are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib4 v4.31.0 (zero sorry placeholders); the Klindt et al. converse is taken as an external premise. The contrast establishes that symbolic grounding in the causal generator of the world's dynamics is the sufficient condition and, in non-Gaussian regimes, the only condition for near-infinite temporal consistency.
tldr: The paper proves that symbolic world models achieve near-infinite temporal consistency for non-Gaussian systems, overcoming a fundamental limit of statistical world models.
motivation: Statistical world models fail for non-Gaussian dynamics, leading to growing representation error over time. The authors aim to show this limit is not fundamental and can be overcome by symbolic grounding.
method: The authors introduce the Physics-Grounded Symbolic Architecture (PGSA) and prove three theorems about identifiability, per-step error bounded by numerical precision, and near-infinite temporal consistency. Four theorems are formalized in Lean 4.
result: PGSA achieves exact linear identifiability for all physical regimes, per-step error bounded by numerical precision, and maintains temporal consistency for an unbounded number of transitions. Statistical world models cannot achieve this for non-Gaussian systems.
conclusion: Symbolic grounding in the causal generator of the world's dynamics is sufficient and, for non-Gaussian regimes, necessary for near-infinite temporal consistency.

title: Network-Based Multi-Layer Model Using Machine Learning For Optimal Vaccine Prioritization In Heterogeneous Populations
authors: Bernard Asamoah Afful Mordecai Opoku Ohemeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work advances epidemic control beyond traditional mass vaccination models by integrating population heterogeneity, network structure, and machine-learning-based decision policies. Using the Email-Eu-core contact network, we compare classical centrality-driven vaccination strategies with graph neural network (GNN) and reinforcement learning (RL) approaches. Across 30 stochastic simulations, classical heuristics, including degree, betweenness, and layer-based vaccination, exhibit similar performance, reflecting the network's dense connectivity and modest community structure. In contrast, the GNN-based strategy substantially reduces peak infection, final epidemic size, and time to peak, demonstrating its ability to identify structurally critical nodes that classical metrics overlook. These results show that learning-based vaccination policies can significantly outperform traditional heuristics by exploiting higher-order relational patterns in real-world networks, offering a powerful framework for targeted epidemic intervention.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning (GNN and RL) to optimize vaccine prioritization in a contact network, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Traditional mass vaccination models ignore population heterogeneity and network structure, leading to suboptimal epidemic control.
method: The authors compare classical centrality-based vaccination strategies with GNN and RL approaches on the Email-Eu-core contact network, using 30 stochastic simulations.
result: GNN-based strategy significantly reduces peak infection, final epidemic size, and time to peak compared to classical heuristics.
conclusion: Learning-based vaccination policies can outperform traditional heuristics by exploiting higher-order relational patterns in real-world networks.

title: Sovereign Stress Avalanches And Network Amplification In Latin America
authors: Diego Vallarino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies sovereign stress avalanches and network amplification in Latin American credit markets using monthly J.P. Morgan EMBI Global Diversified spreads for eleven sovereigns over 2007-2026. Country stress events are defined as positive log-spread innovations exceeding country-specific volatility thresholds, and regional avalanches count the number of stressed countries in each month. The empirical design combines finite-sample power-law diagnostics, threshold robustness checks, a country-level reshuffling placebo, and rolling correlation, partial-correlation, and minimum-spanning-tree networks. Avalanche sizes are heavy-tailed, with an estimated exponent of 1.77, while spread changes and inter-event times lie in a heavy-tail boundary regime. The placebo shows synchronization far above independent stress timing, with p-values below 0.001. Large avalanches coincide with denser and more spectrally amplifying raw-correlation networks, but not after partial-correlation filtering, indicating common-factor co-movement rather than conditional regional propagation. Network metrics describe contemporaneous stress regimes rather than early-warning signals. The results provide a finite-size criticality framework for monitoring sovereign fragility in emerging markets.
tldr: This paper studies sovereign stress avalanches and network amplification in Latin American credit markets using financial data and network analysis.
motivation: To understand systemic risk and contagion in emerging market sovereign debt.
method: Uses EMBI spreads, defines stress events via volatility thresholds, applies power-law diagnostics, placebo tests, and rolling correlation/partial-correlation networks.
result: Avalanche sizes are heavy-tailed with exponent 1.77; synchronization far exceeds independent timing; large avalanches correlate with denser raw-correlation networks but not after partial-correlation filtering.
conclusion: Network metrics describe contemporaneous stress regimes rather than early-warning signals; results provide a finite-size criticality framework for monitoring sovereign fragility.

title: A Systematic Review Of Covid-19 Epidemic Models With Endogenous Human Behaviour. What's Next?
authors: Elena D'agnese, Alessia Melegaro, Vittoria Offeddu, Alberto D'onofrio, Nicola Perra, Chris T. Bauch, Piero Manfredi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human behaviour and epidemic dynamics are intertwined, yet accounting for this feedback remains one of the key challenges of epidemiological modelling. The COVID-19 pandemic was an opportunity to overcome the traditional limitations of the field, raising expectations that data-informed endogenous approaches to behaviour modelling would advance substantially. To quantify the progresses made, we conducted a systematic review of SARS-CoV-2 transmission models endogenously including human behaviour in response to epidemic dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic saw great strides in terms of the expanded use of empirical data in epi-behavioural modelling. However, it also showed shortcomings with respect to limited use of behavioural empirical data, lack of innovation in model structure, and limited engagement with other disciplines and decision-makers. Overall, our results suggest that identifying priorities in model design and behavioural data, building an adequate data collection infrastructure, leveraging on AI advancements, and fostering interdisciplinarity are strategies of utmost importance for pandemic preparedness.
tldr: A systematic review of COVID-19 epidemic models that incorporate endogenous human behavior, highlighting progress and shortcomings.
motivation: To quantify advances in epidemiological modeling during the COVID-19 pandemic, specifically regarding the integration of human behavior feedback.
method: Systematic review of SARS-CoV-2 transmission models that endogenously include human behavior in response to epidemic dynamics.
result: The pandemic saw expanded use of empirical data but limited innovation in model structure and engagement with other disciplines.
conclusion: Priorities for pandemic preparedness include better model design, behavioral data infrastructure, AI advancements, and interdisciplinarity.

title: Feature-preserving Latent-EnKF For Data Assimilation Of Flows With Shocks
authors: Hemanth Chandravamsi, Hangchuan Hu, Ponkrshnan Thiagarajan, Tamer A. Zaki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is widely adopted for sequential data assimilation, but fails for solutions with discontinuities, such as shocks in compressible flows. Uncertainty in shock location induces multimodal ensemble statistics that violate the Gaussian assumptions underlying the EnKF, producing large-scale spurious oscillations in the analysis state. We introduce a feature-preserving latent-EnKF that performs the ensemble update in a learned low-dimensional latent space, where shock and flow features admit a smooth manifold representation, thereby preserving sharp features during EnKF analysis. The updated latent state is mapped back to physical state through a shared decoder for all ensemble members. The algorithm eliminates the member-specific ordered training and positivity flooring used in prior approaches. Numerical experiments on a Sod shock tube and Mach 2 shock interaction with a 2D cylinder, using sparse and noisy observations, show accurate feature recovery of shocks and contact discontinuities without spurious oscillations.
tldr: This paper presents a feature-preserving latent-EnKF method for data assimilation of flows with shocks, using a learned latent space to handle discontinuities.
motivation: Standard EnKF fails for compressible flows with shocks due to non-Gaussian ensemble statistics, leading to spurious oscillations. The authors aim to preserve sharp features during assimilation.
method: They perform the ensemble update in a learned low-dimensional latent space where shock and flow features are smooth, then map back to physical space via a shared decoder.
result: Numerical experiments on Sod shock tube and Mach 2 shock-cylinder interaction show accurate recovery of shocks and contact discontinuities without spurious oscillations.
conclusion: The latent-EnKF effectively handles discontinuities in data assimilation, outperforming standard EnKF for compressible flows.

title: Scar Dynamics Of Adolescent Substance Use: Peer Influence, Dropout, And Bifurcation Structure In A School-based Model
authors: Tamantha Pizarro, Jinni Su, Yixuan He, Yun Kang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a four-compartment susceptible--casual--addicted--resistant (SCAR) model for adolescent substance use in a high-school setting. The model divides students into susceptible non-users, casual or experimental users, students with sustained or substance-use-disorder (SUD)-level involvement, and resistant students in protective anti-use environments. It includes peer-driven initiation, escalation from casual to problematic use, protective peer influence, school disengagement, and partial re-entry after rehabilitation. Qualitative analysis and bifurcation diagrams show three main results. First, the return parameter \(\phi\) separates two regimes: when \(\phi=1\), the total population is conserved and interior equilibria may exist; when \(\phi<1\), problematic use causes net school-population loss, so positive scaled equilibria may not represent true endemic equilibria. Second, initiation and escalation are governed by distinct thresholds, meaning first use and progression to problematic use are dynamically different. Third, the model can exhibit multistability, including bistability between a substance-free state and a stable high-use state, so long-term outcomes may depend on initial conditions. These findings suggest that effective school policy should combine universal prevention, early intervention for casual users, targeted support for students at risk of problematic use, recovery-supportive environments, and strong school re-engagement pathways.
tldr: This paper models adolescent substance use dynamics in schools using a compartmental SCAR model, analyzing peer influence, dropout, and bifurcation structure.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of substance use among adolescents and inform school-based prevention and intervention policies.
method: Develops a four-compartment susceptible-casual-addicted-resistant (SCAR) model with peer-driven initiation, escalation, protective influence, school disengagement, and re-entry, analyzed via qualitative analysis and bifurcation diagrams.
result: Identifies two regimes separated by a return parameter, distinct thresholds for initiation and escalation, and multistability including bistability between substance-free and high-use states.
conclusion: Effective school policy should combine universal prevention, early intervention, targeted support, recovery environments, and strong re-engagement pathways.

title: A conformally-Euclidean Line Element For Evaluating Color Differences
authors: Patrick de Visschere, Patrick Candry, Kristiaan Neyts
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starting from our previously proposed line element and considering more ``surface color'' datasets, we derive a simplified version which matches experimental datasets equally well and resulted into a conformally-Euclidean line element, which is conceptually much simpler than any existing color difference metrics. The color difference is written as an Euclidean difference multiplied with a simple factor which depends on the luminance only. In a subspace with constant luminance, as considered by MacAdam, this factor becomes constant and the subspace is flat. The same holds for sufficiently large luminances. Based on this LE we derive perceptual coordinates [MATH] very similar to the CIELab [MATH].
tldr: This paper proposes a conformally-Euclidean line element for color difference evaluation, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To derive a simplified and conceptually simpler color difference metric that matches experimental datasets.
method: Starting from a previously proposed line element and considering surface color datasets, the authors derive a conformally-Euclidean line element with a luminance-dependent factor.
result: The resulting line element is conformally-Euclidean, with a flat subspace at constant luminance, and yields perceptual coordinates similar to CIELab.
conclusion: The proposed metric is simpler than existing color difference metrics and matches experimental data well.

title: Distributional Point Values For Borel And Symmetric Borel Derivatives
authors: Subhasis Ray
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Borel and symmetric Borel derivatives are generalized derivatives defined through local averages of difference quotients. Distributional point values, in the sense of {\L}ojasiewicz and its symmetric variants, are a classical way of describing the local value of a distribution. This paper connects these two ideas. Writing [MATH] for the regular distribution generated by [MATH], we prove that finite first and second symmetric Borel derivatives give symmetric distributional point values of [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. For the first symmetric derivative, Borel smoothness is used as a sufficient condition to pass from the symmetric point value to the full {\L}ojasiewicz point value. We also prove that the one-sided Borel derivatives determine the right and left distributional point values of [MATH], and that the ordinary Borel derivative gives the full point value when the two one-sided averages agree. Examples show why the second-order symmetric result cannot be strengthened automatically.
tldr: This paper studies distributional point values for Borel and symmetric Borel derivatives, a topic in pure mathematical analysis.
motivation: To connect generalized derivatives defined via local averages with distributional point values, extending classical results.
method: Uses definitions of Borel and symmetric Borel derivatives and Lojasiewicz point values, proving theorems about their relationships.
result: Finite first and second symmetric Borel derivatives imply symmetric distributional point values; one-sided Borel derivatives determine right/left point values.
conclusion: The connections are established, but second-order symmetric results cannot be automatically strengthened.

title: Cascading Smoothers For Multigrid
authors: Robert I. Saye
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multigrid methods are among the most effective frameworks for solving large-scale sparse systems. However, achieving their hallmark linear scaling and rapid convergence crucially depends on an effective smoother algorithm, whose design is often highly problem-dependent. This paper develops a new approach, referred to as due to their operation as an ordered sequence of single-step block-diagonal smoothers. Each level in the cascade is optimised to maximally damp the output of prior steps via a Frobenius norm minimisation of the corresponding error propagators. In particular, we develop an additive (resp., multiplicative) formulation analogous to Jacobi (resp., Gauss-Seidel). Applied within a standard multigrid V-cycle, we show they are remarkably effective across a wide array of problems, including finite difference, finite element, and discontinuous Galerkin discretisations applied to Poisson, elliptic interface, and Stokes systems as well as multiphase variants. In every case, cascading smoothers closely match or significantly outperform their optimally-damped classical counterparts, yet require no parameter tuning apart from a few discrete solver choices. Additionally, the approach is highly parallelisable and robust to geometric and operator complexities such as unstructured meshes and high-contrast coefficients.
tldr: This paper introduces cascading smoothers for multigrid methods, a numerical linear algebra technique, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Multigrid methods are effective for solving large sparse systems but require problem-dependent smoother design; the authors aim to develop a parameter-free, robust smoother.
method: They propose cascading smoothers that operate as an ordered sequence of single-step block-diagonal smoothers, optimized via Frobenius norm minimization of error propagators.
result: The cascading smoothers match or outperform optimally-damped classical counterparts across various discretizations and problems, with high parallelizability and robustness.
conclusion: Cascading smoothers provide a versatile, parameter-free alternative for multigrid methods, eliminating the need for manual tuning.

title: Hyperbolicity-Preserving Stochastic Galerkin Methods For Conservation Laws Based On Associative Truncated Products On Polynomial Spaces
authors: Yulong Xing Haroun Meghaichi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Galerkin discretizations of nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws may lose hyperbolicity because the standard pseudospectral product is generally nonassociative, leading to non-commuting blocks in the flux Jacobian matrix. We develop a novel framework for constructing hyperbolicity-preserving stochastic Galerkin systems based on associative truncated products on polynomial spaces. In one stochastic dimension, we characterize associative truncated products through a single polynomial datum and identify examples with useful symmetry, positivity, and spectral properties, including collocation products and an associative symmetric product based on Gaussian quadrature nodes. We prove a consistency result showing that, under suitable projection-error assumptions, these products converge to the classical product as the polynomial degree grows. For systems with rational fluxes, we derive sufficient conditions under which the resulting stochastic Galerkin flux remains hyperbolic on the corresponding admissible set. Applications to the one-dimensional isothermal and compressible Euler equations show accurate statistical approximation and robust hyperbolicity preservation of the computed stochastic Galerkin states.
tldr: This paper develops hyperbolicity-preserving stochastic Galerkin methods for conservation laws using associative truncated products on polynomial spaces.
motivation: Standard stochastic Galerkin discretizations of nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws can lose hyperbolicity due to nonassociative pseudospectral products, leading to non-commuting blocks in the flux Jacobian.
method: The authors characterize associative truncated products on polynomial spaces via a single polynomial datum and construct examples with useful properties, including collocation and symmetric products based on Gaussian quadrature nodes.
result: They prove consistency and derive sufficient conditions for hyperbolicity preservation in systems with rational fluxes, demonstrating accurate statistical approximation and robust hyperbolicity on the isothermal and compressible Euler equations.
conclusion: The proposed framework ensures hyperbolicity preservation in stochastic Galerkin methods, enabling reliable uncertainty quantification for nonlinear conservation laws.

title: On The Completeness Of Generalized Hierarchical Spline Spaces
authors: Ahmed Oufqir, Carla Manni, Hendrik Speleers
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a general theoretical approach to hierarchical spline spaces that replaces the classical constructive definition - based on basis selection - with a descriptive formulation in terms of regularity constraints. Specifically, we define generalized hierarchical spline spaces on multi-level domains as collections of piecewise functions satisfying hierarchical contact conditions across interfaces between refinement levels. The proposed framework applies to a broad class of local function spaces and relies on a minimal abstract requirement, the extension assumption, rather than on specific polynomial properties. Within this framework, we identify rules under which the hierarchical selection mechanism yields a complete basis, in the sense that it spans exactly the space characterized by the contact conditions. As an application, we consider Tchebycheffian spline spaces. We show that spaces generated by extended complete Tchebycheff (ECT) systems fit in this framework, thereby establishing the completeness of hierarchical Tchebycheffian splines. This demonstrates that the proposed theory naturally extends beyond the polynomial setting and provides a unified foundation for hierarchical constructions in more general spline spaces.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for generalized hierarchical spline spaces, focusing on completeness conditions and extending to Tchebycheffian splines.
motivation: To provide a descriptive formulation of hierarchical spline spaces based on regularity constraints rather than basis selection, enabling a unified theory for broader spline classes.
method: The authors define hierarchical spline spaces via contact conditions and prove completeness under an extension assumption, then apply the framework to ECT systems.
result: They establish rules for complete basis generation and show that hierarchical Tchebycheffian splines fit the framework, proving their completeness.
conclusion: The proposed theory generalizes hierarchical spline constructions beyond polynomials, offering a unified foundation for various spline spaces.

title: A Communication Complexity Lower Bound For Nonuniformly Convex Consensus Optimization
authors: Maxim Klimenko Demyan Yarmoshik
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the communication complexity of convex decentralized optimization over time-varying networks, where [MATH] nodes hold private functions and must agree on the global minimizer using only synchronous exchanges with neighbors. The cost is the number of communication rounds to reach accuracy [MATH] -- a measure akin to round complexity in the LOCAL model, but constrained by nodes sharing only oracle responses. We prove a new lower bound of [MATH] communication rounds, where [MATH] is the condition number of the network Laplacians and [MATH] that of the global objective, showing the round complexity attainable under uniform regularity cannot be matched in the nonuniform regime. The construction rests on spectral graph theory: we embed time-rotating star gadgets into the edges of an expander and patch them to preserve spectral connectivity.
tldr: This paper proves a communication complexity lower bound for nonuniformly convex decentralized optimization over time-varying networks.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental communication cost of distributed optimization is important for designing efficient algorithms, especially when objective functions have varying condition numbers across nodes.
method: The authors use spectral graph theory to construct a hard instance by embedding time-rotating star gadgets into an expander graph, preserving spectral connectivity while forcing high communication rounds.
result: They prove a lower bound of Ω(√(κ_L) log(1/ε)) communication rounds, where κ_L is the condition number of the network Laplacians and κ is that of the global objective, showing that the round complexity under uniform regularity cannot be matched in the nonuniform regime.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental limitation for decentralized optimization in nonuniform settings, highlighting the impact of network topology and function heterogeneity on communication efficiency.

title: The Three Dimensional Neumann Green's Function For General Surfaces: Singular Asymptotics And Boundary Integral Methods
authors: Alan E. Lindsay, Andrew J. Bernoff, Tristan Goodwill, Jeremy G. Hoskins
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an asymptotic analysis and high-order boundary integral method for the three-dimensional Neumann Green's function in general geometries. The Neumann Green's function is a fundamental quantity which arises in numerous fields of science and engineering. In the application of singular perturbation methods to strongly localized reactions and diffusive transport, the Green's function plays the key role in mediating global dynamics. However, this essential quantity can only be determined in closed form for a limited set of geometries. The Green's function for the Laplacian is an elliptic problem with a Dirac forcing term. Accurate resolution of the solution requires a careful decomposition into a singular and a regular part. The bulk scenario is where the source is placed off surface and the singularity is given by the free-space function. In the surface case, where the source is placed at a curved point on the boundary, we use asymptotic analysis to determine a three-term singularity structure. With explicit knowledge of these singularities, we develop a high-order boundary integral method for the determination of the remaining regular part. To resolve the singular boundary data, our integral method uses a custom discretization with Duffy patches near the source. We validate our method using several test cases in which closed form solutions can be developed, including spheres, prolate spheroids and constructed domains. We demonstrate the applicability of our method to address some open problems in narrow capture theory.
tldr: This paper develops asymptotic analysis and high-order boundary integral methods for the three-dimensional Neumann Green's function on general surfaces, with applications to narrow capture theory.
motivation: The Neumann Green's function is fundamental in many fields but can only be solved analytically for simple geometries; numerical methods are needed for general surfaces.
method: The authors decompose the solution into singular and regular parts, derive a three-term singularity expansion for surface sources, and use a boundary integral method with Duffy patches to resolve singularities.
result: They validate the method on spheres, prolate spheroids, and constructed domains, demonstrating high-order accuracy and applicability to narrow capture problems.
conclusion: The method provides an accurate and efficient way to compute the Neumann Green's function on arbitrary surfaces, enabling studies of localized reactions and diffusive transport.

title: Finite-sheeted Cauchy Operator At Rational Corners
authors: Louis Shuo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Cauchy singular integral operators on planar wedges whose opening angle is a rational multiple of [MATH]. For [MATH], the covering [MATH] yields an exact finite-sheeted factorization of the wedge Cauchy transform into [MATH] interval Cauchy transforms with explicit algebraic recombination coefficients. The factorization is formulated on weighted conormal H\"older spaces. We prove that the lifting operator preserves conormal order, lowers the H\"older exponent from [MATH] to [MATH], and has sharp [MATH] sheet norm [MATH]. Combining this operator factorization with a Mellin model for interval Cauchy transforms, we derive a mode-by-mode propagation rule for polyhomogeneous endpoint expansions. Nonresonant powers preserve their logarithmic order, while integer exponents raise it by one. The results also give a local singular decomposition for Cauchy operators on piecewise analytic curves with rational corner angles.
tldr: The paper studies Cauchy singular integral operators on planar wedges with rational opening angles, focusing on operator factorization and endpoint expansions.
motivation: To understand the behavior of Cauchy operators on piecewise analytic curves with rational corner angles, which is a problem in classical analysis.
method: Uses finite-sheeted covering maps to factorize the wedge Cauchy transform into interval Cauchy transforms, and employs a Mellin model for interval operators.
result: Derives a mode-by-mode propagation rule for polyhomogeneous endpoint expansions, showing that nonresonant powers preserve logarithmic order while integer exponents raise it by one.
conclusion: Provides a local singular decomposition for Cauchy operators on piecewise analytic curves with rational corner angles.

title: Constructive Notes On Locally Convex Spaces
authors: Douglas S. Bridges
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a detailed, corrected presentation of some fundamentals of the constructive theory of locally convex spaces that appear without proofs in <cite>BVtech</cite>. This suffices for some important functional analytic theorems that are stated in our final section.
tldr: This paper presents a constructive treatment of locally convex spaces, a topic in functional analysis, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a detailed, corrected presentation of fundamentals of constructive locally convex space theory that were previously stated without proof.
method: Constructive mathematical proofs and exposition of key theorems in locally convex spaces.
result: A corrected and detailed exposition of constructive locally convex space theory, sufficient for important functional analytic theorems.
conclusion: The paper contributes to constructive functional analysis but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Abstract Dynamic Programming On Partially Ordered Spaces
authors: Chengyuan Peng, John Stachurski, Jingni Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study abstract dynamic programs on partially ordered spaces, pairing the order-theoretic approach to dynamic programming with topological and metric foundations. We show that readily verifiable forms of topological stability, such as global stability and contractivity of the policy operators, deliver the fundamental optimality properties of dynamic programming together with convergence of value function iteration, Howard policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration. We also prove that stationary policies dominate nonstationary policy plans under very weak assumptions. Applications include Markov decision processes, structural estimation problems in which maximization and integration are interchanged, optimal stopping without discounting, and Bayesian sequential analysis. For the last two, our results weaken existing assumptions and extend algorithmic guarantees for foundational problems.
tldr: This paper studies abstract dynamic programming on partially ordered spaces, focusing on topological stability and convergence of policy iteration methods.
motivation: To extend dynamic programming theory to partially ordered spaces and provide convergence guarantees for value and policy iteration under weak assumptions.
method: The authors use order-theoretic and topological foundations, proving that global stability and contractivity of policy operators yield optimality and convergence.
result: They show that stationary policies dominate nonstationary ones under weak assumptions, and apply results to Markov decision processes, optimal stopping, and Bayesian sequential analysis.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for dynamic programming on partially ordered spaces, weakening existing assumptions and extending algorithmic guarantees.

title: A Variable Time-step, Second-order, And MBP-preserving Linear Stabilized Scheme For The Time-fractional Allen-Cahn Equation
authors: Bingyin Zhang, Ao Zhang, Hongfei Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a second-order linear scheme based on the variable-step Alikhanov formula and central difference discretization for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation. The nonlinear potential is treated explicitly via a second-order extrapolation with preprocessing, which enables the discrete maximum-bound principle (MBP) to be preserved through an appropriate stabilization technique. Moreover, by developing a discrete fractional Gr\"onwall inequality together with the uniform boundedness of numerical solutions guaranteed by the MBP, we establish an [MATH]-robust and optimal second-order maximum-norm error estimate under initial weak singularity assumption. In addition, energy stability is proved in the sense that the discrete original energy is uniformly bounded by the initial energy plus a high-order spatiotemporal correction term. Finally, extensive numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation, focusing on preserving the maximum-bound principle and energy stability.
motivation: The time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation models phase separation with memory effects, and efficient numerical methods that preserve physical properties are needed.
method: A second-order linear scheme using variable-step Alikhanov formula and central difference, with explicit treatment of nonlinear potential via extrapolation and stabilization to preserve MBP.
result: The scheme is MBP-preserving, second-order accurate, and energy stable, with rigorous error estimates under initial weak singularity.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is effective for simulating the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: Massively Parallel Flow Routing And Drainage Area Determination
authors: Wolfgang Bangerth
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital elevation models (DEMs) have reached resolutions and sizes that only parallel computaters can efficiently process. One important application of DEMs is predicting how much water flows where, the so-called ``flow routing problem'' (a variation of which is the problem of determining the drainage area upstream of a point in a DEM). The traditional algorithm for flow routing is sequential, and attempts to parallelize this method have so far only been moderately successful. Herein, we build on earlier work in Richardson et al. (2014) and propose an algorithm and several variations that can efficiently solve the flow routing problem on very large models with very large numbers of parallel processes. For the largest model we use, with 1.88 billion points, the best algorithm herein can route water in 4.0 seconds on 12,288 processes of a computer cluster.
tldr: This paper presents a massively parallel algorithm for flow routing and drainage area determination in digital elevation models.
motivation: Digital elevation models have grown too large for sequential processing, necessitating efficient parallel algorithms for hydrological modeling.
method: The authors build on prior work to develop and optimize parallel algorithms for flow routing, tested on up to 12,288 processes and models with 1.88 billion points.
result: The best algorithm routes water in 4.0 seconds on 12,288 processes for the largest model, demonstrating high scalability.
conclusion: The proposed parallel algorithms enable efficient processing of very large digital elevation models for flow routing.

title: Local Consistency And Higher-Order Structure Of Spherical Interpolation
authors: Shingyu Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spherical Interpolation of orDER [MATH] (SIDER-[MATH]) is a recursive high-order interpolation construction for data on the unit sphere [MATH], built from repeated spherical linear interpolation (SLERP). This paper gives a local consistency analysis of SIDER for smooth spherical curves sampled at equally spaced parameter values. The analysis is carried out in geodesic normal coordinates, which allows the SIDER recursion to be compared with classical Neville interpolation while retaining the curvature-dependent corrections introduced by SLERP. We first derive local expansions of SLERP and show that SIDER2 has third-order accuracy; its leading error has the same shifted nodal structure as Euclidean quadratic interpolation. We then prove that the adjacent SIDER2 errors entering SIDER3 have a common leading coefficient, so that the SIDER3 recurrence cancels the cubic term and yields fourth-order accuracy. Carrying the expansion one order further gives the corresponding coefficient compatibility for SIDER3 and proves fifth-order accuracy of SIDER4. Finally, we introduce a degree-filtered formal expansion framework for the general SIDER recursion. This framework proves that, for each fixed [MATH], SIDER-[MATH] preserves the required polynomial degree structure in the normalized stencil variable. Together with the interpolation conditions at the [MATH] nodes, this yields the local consistency estimate [MATH] under the stated smoothness and small-stencil assumptions.
tldr: This paper presents a local consistency analysis of a recursive spherical interpolation method (SIDER) for data on the unit sphere, proving high-order accuracy.
motivation: To understand the accuracy and error structure of spherical interpolation methods, which are important for applications in computer graphics, robotics, and numerical analysis on manifolds.
method: The analysis uses geodesic normal coordinates to compare SIDER with classical Neville interpolation, deriving local expansions of SLERP and proving error cancellation in the recursion.
result: SIDER2 has third-order accuracy, SIDER3 fourth-order, and SIDER4 fifth-order; a general framework proves that SIDER-k preserves polynomial degree structure and achieves k+1 order accuracy.
conclusion: The SIDER family provides high-order accurate interpolation on spheres, with error structure analogous to Euclidean interpolation but with curvature-dependent corrections.

title: A Quaternion--BCH Framework For The Local Accuracy Of Sider Interpolation
authors: Shingyu Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spherical Interpolation of orDER [MATH] (SIDER-[MATH]) is a recursive high-order interpolation method for data on the unit sphere [MATH], built from repeated spherical linear interpolation (SLERP). This paper develops a quaternion--Lie algebra framework for proving the local consistency of SIDER for smooth spherical curves sampled at equally spaced parameter values. Points on [MATH] are represented as pure unit quaternions, and interpolation errors are measured in fixed-base quaternion logarithmic coordinates. In this setting, each SLERP operation admits an exact Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) representation, which converts the geometric interpolation problem into an algebraic problem involving filtered Lie-polynomial expansions. The BCH expansion shows that SLERP is affine to leading order, has no quadratic correction, and has a first nonlinear correction that is cubic and commutator-valued. Using this structure, we prove that SIDER2 has a third-order divided-error form with the same leading nodal factor as ordinary quadratic interpolation. We then show that the recursive SIDER step raises the order by one: the affine part gives the Neville-type finite-difference cancellation, while the nonlinear BCH remainder preserves the sharp filtered degree structure after the nodal factor is removed. Consequently, for every fixed [MATH], [MATH]under the stated smoothness and small-stencil assumptions. The proof also identifies the shift-invariance of the leading divided-error coefficient as the algebraic compatibility condition underlying the SIDER recurrence.
tldr: This paper develops a quaternion-Lie algebra framework to prove the local consistency of a spherical interpolation method (SIDER) for data on the unit sphere.
motivation: To provide a rigorous proof of the local accuracy of SIDER interpolation for smooth spherical curves, which is needed for applications in geometry processing and computer graphics.
method: Points on the sphere are represented as pure unit quaternions, and interpolation errors are analyzed using quaternion logarithmic coordinates and the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula to convert geometric interpolation into algebraic Lie-polynomial expansions.
result: The BCH expansion shows SLERP is affine to leading order with cubic commutator-valued correction; SIDER2 achieves third-order divided-error form, and the recursive SIDER step raises the order by one.
conclusion: The framework proves that SIDER achieves the expected order of accuracy under smoothness and small-stencil assumptions, with shift-invariance of the leading error coefficient enabling the recurrence.

title: Maximum Utility Split Method For Utility Preference Elicitation
authors: Bo Chen, Jia Liu, Huifu Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach, called maximum utility split (MUS) scheme, which is built on random utility split (RUS) scheme but with a notable difference: one lottery is designed with two fixed outcomes but with varying probability, and the other has a deterministic outcome specifically chosen at the point where the range between the largest and smallest possible utility values is maximized. Consequently, the probability of random lottery is set such that the range of the ambiguity set of utility functions is reduced by half at the point. Under moderate conditions, we show that MUS can successively generate a sequence of such questionnaires and effectively reduce the ambiguity set, eventually converging to the true utility function as the number of questionnaires increases. The main challenge is to effectively identify the point with the largest utility range for a given ambiguity set constructed from preference information. Based on the structure of the ambiguity set, we propose an interval-based algorithm which identifies each certain-outcome lottery by solving a sequence of linear programs. Moreover, to deal with the case where elicitation terminates before the ambiguity set reduces to a singleton, we demonstrate how to figure out a nominal utility function by solving optimization programs. These identify the smallest and largest utility functions under the Kantorovich metric within the ambiguity set, after which we identify a nominal utility function located in the middle of them. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the efficiency of the MUS method and the performance of a robo-advisor system based on MUS-type queries and the nominal utility elicitation. While the main discussions focus on concave utility functions, we also demonstrate how the MUS approach can be extended to accommodate general non-concave utility functions, particularly S-shaped ones.
tldr: This paper proposes a maximum utility split method for utility preference elicitation, using adaptive questionnaires to converge to the true utility function.
motivation: Existing utility elicitation methods may be inefficient or require many queries; the authors aim to design a more efficient scheme that reduces the ambiguity set of utility functions.
method: The MUS scheme adaptively selects lotteries that maximize the range of possible utility values, reducing the ambiguity set by half each step, and uses linear programming to identify optimal certain-outcome lotteries.
result: Under moderate conditions, the method converges to the true utility function as the number of questionnaires increases, and a nominal utility function can be extracted when elicitation terminates early.
conclusion: The MUS approach efficiently elicits utility preferences and can be extended to non-concave utility functions, with potential applications in robo-advisor systems.

title: Pinching-Antenna Enabled Multicell Wireless Systems
authors: Yunshu Chen, Qing Xue, Meng Hua, Bingpeng Zhou, Shaodan Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching antenna (PA) systems have recently emerged as a promising flexible-antenna technology, which can reconstruct the wireless propagation environment by dynamically adjusting the positions of pinching elements along dielectric waveguides, thereby providing new spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) for enhancing wireless system performance. This paper investigates a multi-waveguide PA-based multi-cell communication system, focusing on the joint optimization of precoding matrices, waveguide power allocation, and antenna placement to maximize the weighted sum rate (WSR). In multi-cell scenarios, inter-cell interference typically leads to a highly coupled and nonconvex WSR maximization problem. To address this challenge, an efficient alternating optimization framework is adopted to optimize each variable in an iterative way. Specifically, fractional programming is first employed to reformulate the original problem by introducing auxiliary variables that decouple the signal and interference terms. Based on this reformulation, block coordinate descent is then applied to optimize the precoding matrices and power allocation, leading to closed-form or semi-closed-form updates. For the high-dimensional and nonconvex PA placement problem, particle swarm optimization (PSO) is utilized to perform an efficient search and improve scalability. Numerical results demonstrate that, under various system configurations, the proposed scheme significantly outperforms baseline methods, including average power allocation, fixed antenna placement, conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), and massive MIMO. These results highlight the strong potential of PA systems for large-scale multi-cell wireless communications.
tldr: This paper optimizes precoding, power allocation, and antenna placement in pinching-antenna multi-cell wireless systems to maximize weighted sum rate.
motivation: Pinching antennas offer new spatial degrees of freedom for wireless communications, but inter-cell interference in multi-cell scenarios poses a challenging nonconvex optimization problem.
method: An alternating optimization framework using fractional programming and block coordinate descent for precoding and power allocation, and particle swarm optimization for antenna placement.
result: The proposed scheme significantly outperforms baseline methods including average power allocation, fixed antenna placement, conventional MIMO, and massive MIMO.
conclusion: Pinching-antenna systems show strong potential for large-scale multi-cell wireless communications.

title: Phase Transition Of Schott's Statistic For High-dimensional Heavy-tailed Data
authors: Hantao Chen, Guangming Pan, Cheng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider Schott's statistic (Schott, 2005) defined as the squared Frobenius norm of the sample correlation matrix for data from [MATH]-regularly varying populations. We investigate its asymptotic distribution in a general framework characterized by data dimension p, sample size n, and regularly varying coefficients [MATH]. In particular, we identify a phase transition phenomenon in the asymptotic behavior. For light-tailed populations ([MATH]), we revisit the [MATH]-free asymptotic distribution but relax the constraint on the ratio of [MATH]. For heavy-tailed populations ([MATH]), we derive a new asymptotic normal distribution whose variance explicitly depends on [MATH]. We also propose a consistent estimator for the asymptotic variance such that the standardized Schott's test statistic remains applicable for unknown location parameters and all [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic distribution of Schott's statistic for high-dimensional heavy-tailed data, identifying a phase transition in its behavior.
motivation: Understanding the asymptotic properties of correlation-based statistics under heavy-tailed distributions is important for high-dimensional statistical inference.
method: The authors analyze Schott's statistic under a general framework with regularly varying tails, deriving asymptotic distributions for light-tailed and heavy-tailed regimes using random matrix theory and extreme value theory.
result: They find a phase transition: for light-tailed populations the asymptotic distribution is free of the tail index, while for heavy-tailed populations it is normal with variance depending on the tail index.
conclusion: The work provides a consistent estimator for the asymptotic variance, enabling practical application of Schott's test for unknown location parameters and all tail indices.

title: Trace Spectra Of Simplices In Large Sets
authors: Michael Bj\"orklund, Alexander Fish, Shrey Sanadhya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an ordered tuple [MATH] of vectors in [MATH], let [MATH] be its edge matrix. We prove that, in every finite colouring of [MATH], one colour class realizes every prescribed value of the higher characteristic coefficients \[ (c_2(A_{\mathbf v}),\ldots,c_d(A_{\mathbf v})). \] This extends Graham's theorem on volumes, which corresponds to the last coefficient [MATH]. We also prove a discrete analogue: if [MATH] has positive upper Banach density, then, for some [MATH], the set of coefficient tuples realized by ordered tuples in [MATH] contains \[ q^2\times q^3\times\cdots\times q^d. \] Finally, we show that the ordinary trace [MATH] cannot be added to these conclusions. The proof combines a quantitative directional expansion result for ergodic actions of free abelian groups with a trace calculation for a family of model edge matrices.
tldr: This paper studies combinatorial geometry and ergodic theory of simplices in large sets, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to extend Graham's theorem on volumes to higher characteristic coefficients of edge matrices of simplices in finite colorings of Euclidean space.
method: The proof combines a quantitative directional expansion result for ergodic actions of free abelian groups with a trace calculation for a family of model edge matrices.
result: They prove that in any finite coloring of R^d, one color class realizes every prescribed tuple of higher characteristic coefficients, and a discrete analogue for sets of positive upper Banach density.
conclusion: The ordinary trace cannot be added to these conclusions, and the results are purely combinatorial/ergodic with no quantum or thermodynamic implications.

title: A Robust Helmholtz-Decomposition-Based Real Compressed Layer Method For Time-Harmonic Elastic Wave Scattering
authors: Lu Zhang Li-Lian Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-harmonic elastic wave scattering involves both compressional (P-) and shear (S-) waves, which propagate with different wavenumbers and polarization characteristics. The naive construction of perfectly matched layer (PML)-type methods based on complex coordinate stretching may lack robustness, or even fail, particularly when the wavenumbers are highly contrasted. The recently developed real compressed layer (RCL) technique build upon real compression transformations and explicit extraction of resulting oscillatory patterns for time-harmonic Helmholtz problems may not work, since the oscillations cannot be explicitly extracted by a single change of variables. This paper intends to bridge this gap by developing a robust RCL method for two-dimensional time-harmonic elastic wave scattering in unbounded domains with compactly supported inhomogeneities. A key observation is that, through the Helmholtz decomposition, the displacement field in the exterior homogeneous region decoupled into P-wave and S-wave and each has a distinctive separation of its oscillatory pattern and decaying behaviours in polar coordinates. We then apply the real compression coordinate transformation in the radial direction to each component. We further propose a coupled displacement-potential RCL formulation that seamlessly integrates the Helmholtz-decomposed wave components with the interior displacement field. We show that, under this framework, the essential oscillations in the layer can be effectively removed. We prove the well-posedness of the resulting coupled problem and establish the exponential convergence of the RCL solution to the original scattering solution in the truncated domain of interest. We discretize the RCL-system using high-order spectral element method and demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method through ample numerical results.
tldr: This paper develops a robust real compressed layer method for time-harmonic elastic wave scattering using Helmholtz decomposition.
motivation: Existing PML-type methods for elastic wave scattering may fail when wavenumbers are highly contrasted, and the RCL technique for Helmholtz problems cannot be directly applied due to multiple wave types.
method: The authors apply Helmholtz decomposition to separate P- and S-waves, then use real compression coordinate transformations in the radial direction for each component, coupled with a displacement-potential formulation.
result: The method effectively removes essential oscillations in the layer, and the authors prove well-posedness and exponential convergence of the RCL solution.
conclusion: The proposed RCL method is robust and effective for two-dimensional time-harmonic elastic wave scattering, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: Flyby Distance Pursuit For Guarding A Target With An Inferior Guard
authors: Navot Israeli, Vitaly Shaferman, Oded Golan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Guarding a target against a fast Attacker with a slower Guard is posed as a differential game. Both players follow nonlinear, thrust-free, aerodynamic motion in the plane. The capturability problem inherent in this scenario is addressed by formulating the game such that the Attacker is constrained to terminate at its Target, and the game value is the flyby distance. The latter is made accessible at termination by introducing an auxiliary state variable that records the players' minimum separation distance throughout their flight. This novel combination of termination condition and auxiliary state removes a structural limitation of current pursuit games and opens a new class of solvable problems. It also enables us to embed attacker mission constraints directly. Taking an indirect approach, we formulate the game's Two-Point Boundary Value Problem, solve it numerically, and identify several solution types. When the Attacker's only constraint is to reach the Target, he can do so without being captured. These types of solutions, however, are less practical due to long flight times and slow terminal speeds. Imposing an Attacker terminal speed constraint yields simpler solutions and reveals the trade-off between terminal speed and flyby distance. We demonstrate that in such a setting, capture is possible in a relevant region of the parameter space.
tldr: This paper studies a differential game of guarding a target with a slower guard, focusing on flyby distance as the game value.
motivation: The authors aim to solve the capturability problem in a pursuit-evasion scenario where a fast attacker must reach a target while a slower guard tries to intercept.
method: They formulate the problem as a differential game with nonlinear aerodynamic motion, introduce an auxiliary state for minimum separation, and solve the two-point boundary value problem numerically.
result: They identify solution types and show that capture is possible when an attacker terminal speed constraint is imposed, revealing trade-offs between speed and flyby distance.
